item.content:encoded:
The University of Sydney offers a range of higher degree by research (HDR) opportunities for students seeking to undertake advanced academic research, including Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Joint PhD, Master’s by Research, and Master of Philosophy (MPhil) programs. These research degrees are designed for students who want to develop substantial expertise in a particular field while conducting an original research project under academic supervision.

For prospective research students, applying successfully involves more than simply submitting an online application. Applicants are expected to demonstrate previous research experience, strong academic performance, the ability to develop a meaningful research proposal, and a suitable relationship with a potential academic supervisor.

This comprehensive guide explains the University of Sydney postgraduate research application process, including eligibility requirements, research proposal development, finding a supervisor, required documents, application timing, scholarships and financial assistance, and additional requirements for international students.

University of Sydney Postgraduate Research Opportunities

A higher degree by research at the University of Sydney can include:

  • Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)
  • Joint PhD programs
  • Master’s by Research
  • Master of Philosophy (MPhil)

The University states that the general application process applies to most research courses and is intended for both domestic and international research students. However, individual faculties and schools may have additional admission requirements or variations in their procedures.

Applicants interested in research degrees in areas such as architecture, arts and social sciences, business, engineering and computer science, law, medicine and health, music, and science should therefore check the requirements of their intended course and faculty carefully.

Important Exception: Sydney Law School and Business School

Applicants interested in postgraduate research through the Sydney Law School or Business School should note that their application process differs from the general process.

For these schools, applicants first apply for their course. If they are successful, a supervisor will then be allocated to them. This differs from the general process, where applicants normally need to secure a supervisor before submitting their application.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

One of the most important parts of preparing an application is determining whether you meet the University’s academic and research requirements.

For postgraduate research study, the University states that applicants need previous research experience and a high academic record.

Previous Research Experience

Applicants should have completed a significant research project or thesis during their previous university-level studies.

Acceptable preparation may include:

  • An Australian honours degree
  • A master’s by research degree
  • A master’s by coursework that includes a substantial thesis or dissertation component

The purpose of this requirement is to demonstrate that applicants have already developed experience conducting academic research and are prepared for the demands of a higher research degree.

This means that prospective PhD or research master’s applicants should not focus only on their final grades. Their previous research experience is also an important part of demonstrating research capability.

Academic Requirements for Postgraduate Research

The University also places considerable importance on academic performance.

For the general postgraduate research requirements, applicants are expected to have a bachelor’s degree with first-class honours, with equivalent standards determined for students from other institutions. The University provides the following guide based on its grading system:

  • WAM of 75 over the degree
  • Honours Class I: WAM greater than 80
  • Honours Class II: WAM between 75 and 80

Equivalent qualifications from other institutions may be assessed according to the University’s requirements.

PhD Eligibility

Applicants seeking admission to a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) need to demonstrate sufficient previous research experience and capability.

In most cases, applicants will have one of the following:

  1. A bachelor’s degree with first-class honours;
  2. A master’s degree completed to a high academic standard that contains a substantial research component; or
  3. An equivalent qualification demonstrating research experience, academic excellence and research capability.

Therefore, prospective PhD applicants should be prepared to demonstrate not only academic excellence but also their ability to undertake independent and substantial research.

Eligibility for a Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy

Applicants interested in a Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy (MPhil) will generally need one of the following:

  • A bachelor’s degree with first- or second-class honours from the University of Sydney or another approved institution; or
  • An equivalent qualification demonstrating sufficient research experience and capability.

Applicants should still check the individual course requirements because specific faculties or programs may have additional admission criteria.

English Language Requirements

English language requirements vary depending on:

  • The specific course;
  • The applicant’s country of origin; and
  • Their previous educational background.

Applicants whose circumstances require proof of English proficiency should determine what evidence is required for their particular course.

International applicants should therefore check the English-language requirements well before submitting their application, particularly if their previous education was not conducted in English.

Joint PhD Opportunities

Students interested in a Joint PhD must initially follow Steps 1 to 3 of the University’s standard PhD application process.

There is an additional process for Joint PhD applicants. The proposed supervisor must complete a proposal to negotiate a student agreement form. If the proposal is accepted, the student must also sign an individual student agreement.

Once the student agreement has been finalised, the applicant will receive an application form for the Joint PhD program.

Applicants interested in this route should therefore allow additional time for discussions with their proposed supervisor and the formalisation of the relevant agreement.

Step 2: Develop a Strong Research Proposal

After establishing eligibility, the next major step is to develop a research proposal.

The University recommends carefully considering the subject of the proposed research project and beginning to develop a proposal that can be shared with potential academic supervisors.

A research proposal is important because it allows you to communicate:

  • What you want to research;
  • Why the topic is important;
  • What you intend to investigate;
  • Why your proposed research is worthwhile;
  • How the project relates to existing academic work; and
  • How your proposed research aligns with the research interests of a potential supervisor.

The University also notes that an initial proposal will likely evolve as discussions with the supervisor progress. Therefore, applicants should not necessarily expect their first version to be the final version.

The important point is to begin with a clear research idea and demonstrate why the proposed project is significant and appropriate for postgraduate research.

Step 3: Find a Suitable Research Supervisor

For most postgraduate research applications at the University of Sydney, applicants need to secure a supervisor before submitting their application.

The main exceptions are applicants to the Sydney Law School and Business School, where students apply for the course first and are allocated a supervisor if successful.

Finding an appropriate supervisor is therefore one of the most important stages of the application.

How to Search for a Supervisor

The University provides Sydney Profiles, where prospective research students can identify academics and explore research supervision opportunities.

Applicants can search using:

  • The name of a particular academic; or
  • A general keyword related to their research area.

For example, an applicant researching a particular scientific or engineering topic could use relevant keywords to identify academics working in that area.

The search can then be refined using filters such as:

  • Faculty and School;
  • Availability; and
  • Research supervision.

Applicants can also combine multiple keywords to make the search more specific.

What to Include When Contacting a Potential Supervisor

Finding an academic whose research interests match your proposed topic is only the beginning. Applicants should prepare a professional enquiry explaining why they are contacting that particular academic.

The University recommends providing information about:

  • Your academic background;
  • Your previous research experience;
  • The research topic you want to investigate;
  • How your proposed research aligns with the supervisor’s research;
  • Your CV or resume;
  • Academic transcripts for all degrees; and
  • Your initial research proposal.

This alignment is particularly important. A strong academic record alone does not necessarily demonstrate that a particular supervisor is suitable for your project. Your proposal should connect meaningfully with the academic’s research interests, projects or expertise.

Step 4: Submit the Application Online

Postgraduate research degree applications at the University of Sydney are open throughout the year.

However, most research intakes begin during:

  • Research Period 2 — March
  • Research Period 3 — July

Applicants should check the research periods available for their specific faculty and course because not every program necessarily follows exactly the same schedule.

The University recommends applying as early as possible before the intended start date.

Applicants should also discuss their intended start date with their proposed supervisor.

Is There a General Application Deadline?

The source does not state one single general deadline for all postgraduate research applications.

Instead, applications are described as being open throughout the year, while individual research periods and funding opportunities may have their own relevant dates.

Important Scholarship Deadline Consideration

Applicants who want to be considered for the Research Training Program (RTP) stipend must submit their application by the relevant RTP dates.

The University explains that applicants may still submit their course application after an RTP deadline, but their stipend outcome will not be provided until the next round of RTP rankings.

Therefore, students seeking funding should not wait until the last possible moment to submit their research degree application.

Deadline: No single general postgraduate research application deadline is stated in the provided source. RTP scholarship applicants must follow the applicable RTP dates.

Documents Required for a University of Sydney Research Degree Application

Once a supervisor has been secured and the research project has been refined, applicants need to prepare the required supporting documentation.

The University identifies several important categories of documents.

1. Research Proposal

The research proposal should be finalised in conjunction with the supervisor.

The University specifies a proposal of up to 2,000 words, covering the objectives and significance of the proposed research.

The proposal should therefore communicate the central purpose and value of the research project clearly.

2. Evidence of Supervisor Agreement

Applicants need evidence that a primary supervisor has agreed to supervise them.

This may take the form of email correspondence showing that the staff member has agreed to supervise the applicant.

The Sydney Conservatorium of Music may have an additional interview requirement.

3. Referee Reports

Applicants must provide two referee reports using the University’s specified forms.

Applicants should therefore identify appropriate academic referees in advance and allow enough time for them to complete and submit their reports.

4. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide official academic transcripts.

These transcripts need to be supplied:

  • In the original language; and
  • With an English translation where applicable.

5. English Language Evidence

Applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency if English is not their first language and the course requires such evidence.

6. CV or Resume

A curriculum vitae or resume is also required as part of the application documentation.

The CV should provide a clear picture of the applicant’s academic background and relevant research experience.

7. Additional Course-Specific Documents

Some courses may require additional materials.

Depending on the program, these could include:

  • A portfolio;
  • An audition; or
  • Other documents specified in the relevant course listing.

Applicants should therefore check their specific degree page rather than assuming that the general documentation list covers every requirement.

General Documents Applicants Need to Prepare

The application also requires proof of identity.

Examples include:

  • A valid passport biodata page;
  • An Australian birth certificate; or
  • An Australian or New Zealand citizenship certificate for domestic students.

Domestic applicants seeking part-time study also need to provide a statement demonstrating that they have sufficient time available to conduct their research under University supervision and complete the degree within the maximum permitted period for part-time PhD enrolment.

Additional Requirements for International Students

International applicants should pay particular attention to the additional requirements associated with studying in Australia.

According to the provided information, international students will need to address immigration and application requirements after receiving an admission offer or an electronic Confirmation of Enrolment (eCoE).

They will need to apply for the appropriate student visa after receiving the necessary admission documentation.

Application Processing Fee

International applicants are also required to pay a non-refundable application processing fee.

However, the source states that this fee can be waived in certain circumstances, including where:

  • The applicant is a sponsored student; or
  • A University staff member grants an exemption during an office interview or recruitment event.

International applicants may also use an authorised University of Sydney agent where appropriate. The University has partnered with authorised agents who can assist with applications and arrangements on behalf of students.

Scholarships and Financial Assistance for Postgraduate Research

Funding is an important consideration for students pursuing research degrees.

The University of Sydney states that it has one of the largest research scholarship schemes in Australia. Research scholarships may help students finance their research or meet living costs while undertaking their studies.

Scholarships may be:

  • Specific to a particular research project;
  • Specific to a particular discipline; or
  • Awarded based on academic merit and research potential.

This means that prospective applicants should investigate available funding opportunities alongside their course application.

Stipend Scholarships

The University also offers competitive stipend scholarships designed to provide an allowance that assists with living costs.

These awards are based on factors including:

  • Academic merit; and
  • Research potential.

Applicants seeking these scholarships must complete the additional scholarship form as part of the course application process.

Funding for Domestic Students

Domestic students do not pay tuition fees and are awarded an RTP Fees Offset under the Australian Government’s Research Training Program.

Funding for International Students

International students are required to pay tuition fees, with fee estimates available through the individual course pages.

However, international applicants can apply for scholarship packages that may provide:

  • A stipend scholarship to assist with relocation and living costs; and
  • A tuition fee scholarship.

These scholarship packages are described as highly competitive and have limited places.

Applicants who require financial assistance should therefore research funding opportunities early and pay close attention to scholarship-specific deadlines.

Research Ethics and Additional Approvals

Some research projects may involve additional ethical or institutional requirements.

For example, applicants conducting research involving fieldwork in the New South Wales hospital and education systems may be required to pass health and security checks. Additional admission criteria may also be specified by the individual course.

Depending on the nature of the research, students may also need approval from relevant ethics committees.

The University specifically notes that research involving human participants or animals may require approval from:

  • The Animal Ethics Committee; and/or
  • The Human Research Ethics Committee.

This is particularly important for applicants whose proposed research involves people, personal information, clinical environments, animals, or other ethically sensitive research activities.

Which Faculties Offer Postgraduate Research Opportunities?

The University provides faculty-specific information for postgraduate research across a wide range of academic disciplines.

Applicants can find additional information for:

  1. Architecture, Design and Planning
  2. Arts and Social Sciences
  3. Business
  4. Engineering and Computer Science
  5. Law
  6. Medicine and Health
  7. Music
  8. Science

Because individual faculties may have different admission requirements or application procedures, prospective students should use the relevant faculty or course page to confirm their requirements before applying.

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Although meeting the formal requirements is essential, prospective applicants should also approach the application strategically.

1. Start With a Clear Research Idea

Before approaching supervisors, develop a research idea that clearly identifies the issue you want to investigate.

Your idea should be specific enough to form the basis of a research project but flexible enough to evolve through discussions with your supervisor.

2. Demonstrate Research Experience

Previous research experience is a major component of the University’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants should therefore clearly communicate relevant:

  • Theses;
  • Dissertations;
  • Research projects;
  • Academic research experience; and
  • Other substantial research work.

3. Choose Supervisors Carefully

Do not simply contact academics because they work within your general discipline.

Instead, look for meaningful overlap between:

Your proposed research + the academic’s research expertise + the academic’s current research projects.

The University specifically encourages applicants to explain how their proposed research aligns with the work of their proposed supervisor.

4. Prepare Your Documents Early

Applicants should begin preparing transcripts, CVs, research proposals, referee reports and evidence of supervisor support well before the intended submission date.

This is especially important for international applicants who may also need to consider English-language evidence, application processing requirements and visa processing times.

The University recommends international applicants factor Department of Home Affairs visa processing times into their planning when considering a likely start date.

5. Consider Funding at the Same Time as Admission

Students who require financial support should not treat scholarship applications as an afterthought.

Because RTP and other scholarship opportunities can have separate deadlines and competitive ranking processes, applicants should investigate funding requirements before submitting their course application.

Application Timeline: What Prospective Students Should Do

A practical approach to the University of Sydney postgraduate research application process is:

Stage 1: Identify your research area

Determine the discipline and broad subject you want to investigate.

Stage 2: Confirm eligibility

Check your academic qualifications, research experience, academic performance and English-language requirements.

Stage 3: Develop an initial research proposal

Create a clear proposal explaining the research problem, objectives and significance.

Stage 4: Search for potential supervisors

Use Sydney Profiles to identify academics whose research interests align with your proposed project.

Stage 5: Contact potential supervisors

Send a professional enquiry accompanied by your CV, transcripts and initial research proposal.

Stage 6: Refine the research project

Work with the prospective supervisor to improve and finalise your research proposal.

Stage 7: Prepare supporting documentation

Gather transcripts, referee reports, proof of English proficiency where required, identity documents and any course-specific materials.

Stage 8: Apply online

Submit your postgraduate research application through the University’s online application process.

Stage 9: Apply for relevant funding

Complete the additional scholarship requirements if you wish to be considered for available research scholarships.

Stage 10: Prepare for additional requirements

International applicants should plan for visa requirements, while applicants whose research involves humans, animals or certain fieldwork environments should consider the relevant ethics and approval requirements.

Deadline for University of Sydney Postgraduate Research Applications

There is no single general deadline stated in the provided source for all postgraduate research degree applications.

Instead, applications are open throughout the year, with research intakes generally taking place in March and July. Applicants are advised to check their specific course and faculty requirements and apply as early as possible before their intended start date.

However, applicants seeking consideration for an RTP stipend must follow the applicable RTP submission dates. Applications submitted after the relevant RTP deadline may still be considered for admission, but the applicant’s stipend outcome will be considered in a subsequent RTP ranking round.

Deadline: No universal postgraduate research application deadline is specified in the source; scholarship applicants should check the applicable RTP and course-specific deadlines.

Who Can Apply?

The University of Sydney’s postgraduate research application process is available to both domestic and international research students.

Academic qualifications

Depending on the degree, applicants generally need:

  • Previous significant research experience;
  • A strong academic record;
  • Appropriate bachelor’s honours or master’s-level qualifications for PhD study; or
  • A bachelor’s degree with first- or second-class honours, or equivalent research capability, for a research master’s/MPhil.

LEARN MORE HERE

Geographic eligibility

The provided source does not identify a restricted list of countries or a particular continent from which applicants must come. It explicitly describes the process as being open to both domestic and international research students.

Race or ethnicity

The provided source does not specify a race or ethnic group restriction for postgraduate research admission.

International applicants

International students can apply, but they may have additional requirements involving:

  • English-language proficiency;
  • Application processing fees;
  • Student visa arrangements;
  • Tuition fees; and
  • Potential international scholarship opportunities.

Conclusion

Pursuing a postgraduate research degree at the University of Sydney can provide an opportunity to undertake advanced independent research through a PhD, Joint PhD, Master’s by Research or Master of Philosophy. However, applicants should understand that the process involves considerably more than completing an online form.

A competitive application begins with the right academic preparation and research experience, followed by the development of a strong research proposal and identification of an appropriate supervisor. Applicants then need to refine their project with their supervisor and prepare the required academic, research and personal documentation before submitting the application.

The University accepts postgraduate research applications throughout the year, although individual courses and research periods may have specific requirements. Students seeking scholarships, particularly RTP funding, need to pay close attention to the relevant funding deadlines because scholarship consideration may operate on a different timeline from general course admission.

For international applicants, additional planning is particularly important because English-language requirements, application fees, tuition costs, scholarships and visa processing may all affect the application timeline.

Ultimately, prospective applicants should begin early, carefully examine their intended course and faculty requirements, identify supervisors whose research aligns with their interests, develop a well-defined proposal, and prepare all supporting documentation before submission. With careful planning, the University of Sydney’s postgraduate research pathway can provide a structured route toward advanced academic research and higher-degree study.

item.content:encoded:
LEAP Africa is inviting experienced, passionate, innovative, and values-driven professionals to explore career opportunities within an organisation focused on youth leadership development and sustainable transformation across Africa. Through its work as an ecosystem builder, thought leader, and development hub, LEAP Africa aims to empower the next generation of African leaders and contribute to lasting impact across communities.

For professionals interested in leadership, youth development, programme management, organisational transformation, and social impact, the organisation offers an opportunity to become part of a dynamic team working to expand its impact across the continent.

Among its current openings is the Director of Programmes position, a senior leadership opportunity based in Lagos, Nigeria.

Opportunity Overview

LEAP Africa describes itself as an institution working beyond the traditional role of an organisation. Its ambition is to serve as an ecosystem builder, thought leader, and development hub for young people across Africa.

The organisation places its people at the centre of this mission and seeks individuals who are prepared to contribute their skills, creativity, ideas, and leadership to initiatives focused on developing young African leaders.

The current Director of Programmes opening is particularly suited to an experienced professional who can provide strategic leadership for LEAP Africa’s programmes and help guide their development in line with the organisation’s priorities for 2027 and beyond.

Key Details

  • Position: Director of Programmes
  • Organisation: LEAP Africa
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Location: Lagos, Nigeria
  • Application deadline: 20 September 2026
  • Application: Applicants can apply through the official application form provided by LEAP Africa.

Apply for the Director of Programmes position

About LEAP Africa

LEAP Africa presents itself as an organisation committed to developing young leaders and supporting sustainable transformation across African communities.

Its work is centred around youth leadership development and creating an environment where young people can be inspired, empowered, and equipped to take on leadership roles.

The organisation describes its broader mission through several interconnected roles:

  • Ecosystem builder: Connecting people, ideas, and initiatives that contribute to development and leadership.
  • Thought leader: Contributing ideas and perspectives around youth leadership and development.
  • Development hub: Creating opportunities and platforms that support the growth of young people.
  • Advocacy champion: Using its experience and platform to promote issues connected to its mission.

Working at LEAP Africa therefore offers professionals the opportunity to contribute to an organisation whose work extends across leadership development and broader social transformation.

Director of Programmes: An Opportunity for Experienced Leaders

The Director of Programmes is described as an experienced and visionary professional who will provide leadership for the organisation’s programmes.

The role involves leading the design, delivery, and growth of LEAP Africa’s programmes while ensuring that these programmes remain aligned with the organisation’s strategic priorities for 2027 and beyond.

This makes the position particularly significant because programme leadership is directly connected to how LEAP Africa implements its mission.

The successful candidate would be joining the organisation at a point where its programmes and strategic direction require leadership capable of supporting continued development and expansion.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Based on the opportunity description, the Director of Programmes will be expected to contribute to:

  1. Programme design

    The role involves leading the development and design of programmes that support LEAP Africa’s broader mission.

  2. Programme delivery

    The Director will provide leadership in ensuring that programmes are effectively implemented.

  3. Programme growth

    The position involves supporting the expansion and growth of LEAP Africa’s programmes.

  4. Strategic alignment

    A major part of the role is ensuring that programmes are aligned with the organisation’s strategic priorities for 2027 and beyond.

  5. Visionary leadership

    LEAP Africa is specifically seeking an experienced and visionary individual, indicating that the position requires more than routine programme administration.

Why Consider a Career at LEAP Africa?

LEAP Africa describes its workplace as one designed to support professional growth, collaboration, employee well-being, and meaningful work.

The organisation identifies several features of its employee experience.

1. Purpose-Driven Work

LEAP Africa places purpose at the centre of its organisational culture.

Employees are connected to work focused on youth leadership development, with the organisation aiming to become a high-performing youth-focused institution and a centre of excellence in key areas of youth leadership development.

For professionals who want their work to contribute to broader social impact, this purpose-driven environment can provide an opportunity to connect professional responsibilities with a wider mission.

2. Benefits and Incentives

LEAP Africa states that it focuses on fair pay, opportunities, and benefits designed to support employees.

The benefits identified by the organisation include:

  • Life insurance
  • Health coverage
  • Competitive compensation
  • Retirement savings
  • Other employee benefits and incentives

These benefits form part of the organisation’s broader approach to supporting its employees.

3. Hybrid Working Structure

LEAP Africa describes itself as a flexible, high-trust workplace.

Its hybrid structure combines:

  • Physical workplace options
  • Remote working options
  • Flexibility in how employees approach work

The organisation recognises that professional and personal life are interconnected and seeks to provide a working structure that accommodates this reality.

4. Professional Reputation and Community

LEAP Africa highlights the pride associated with being part of its community of employees, referred to as LEAPers.

The organisation says its work over the years has positioned it as an ecosystem builder, thought leader, and advocacy champion.

Joining the organisation therefore means becoming part of a professional community connected to its broader leadership-development mission.

5. Learning and Development

Professional development is another component of the employee experience.

LEAP Africa states that it implements policies intended to support employees in developing their:

  • Knowledge
  • Competencies
  • Professional skills

Its learning and development initiatives include learning sessions, an L&D fund, and expert series.

This can provide employees with opportunities to continue developing their capabilities while working within the organisation.

6. Employee Well-being

LEAP Africa describes itself as a people-first organisation and places considerable emphasis on employee well-being and fulfilment.

The organisation mentions:

  • Vacations
  • Public holidays
  • Organisational breaks
  • Wellness days
  • Personal days off
  • Paid annual leave

The goal is to encourage employees to take time away from work and maintain a healthier balance.

7. Collaborative and Dynamic Team

LEAP Africa describes its employees as smart, innovative, creative, and dynamic.

The organisation emphasises:

  • Teamwork
  • Collaboration
  • Mutual support
  • Sharing insights
  • Collective achievement
  • Individual achievement
  • Professional synergy

Professionals joining the organisation can therefore expect to work within a team-oriented environment where collaboration is considered an important part of achieving organisational goals.

LEARN MORE HERE

Join the LEAP Africa Talent Network

In addition to the current Director of Programmes vacancy, LEAP Africa provides an opportunity for interested professionals to join its talent network.

The talent network is intended for people who are interested in becoming part of the LEAP Africa community and want to receive first-hand information about future vacancies and initiatives.

This can be particularly useful for professionals who may not currently be applying for the Director of Programmes position but want to remain informed about future career opportunities with LEAP Africa.

Join the LEAP Africa Talent Network

Who Should Consider This Opportunity?

The current opening is especially relevant to professionals who have experience in areas connected to programme leadership, youth development, organisational development, social impact, and strategic programme management.

The position’s description specifically calls for an experienced and visionary Director of Programmes, meaning applicants should carefully evaluate whether their professional background demonstrates the level of experience and leadership expected for a senior programme position.

Professionals who are passionate about youth leadership development and expanding development-focused programmes across Africa may find the organisation’s mission particularly relevant.

Who Qualifies to Apply?

Category of people: Experienced professionals and senior programme leaders interested in youth leadership development and social impact.

Qualifications/experience: The provided opportunity description does not specify a detailed academic degree requirement, minimum number of years of experience, or specific professional qualifications for the Director of Programmes position. It does, however, explicitly seek an experienced and visionary professional capable of leading programme design, delivery, growth, and strategic alignment.

Geographical eligibility: The position is based in Lagos, Nigeria. The provided information does not explicitly state a nationality restriction or specify that applicants must be Nigerian citizens.

Race/continent: No race-based eligibility restriction is stated. LEAP Africa’s broader mission focuses on young people across Africa, but the supplied vacancy information does not provide a specific nationality or citizenship requirement for this particular position.

Applicants should therefore review the official application information carefully to determine whether additional requirements are included in the application form.

How to Apply

Interested professionals should submit their application through the application form provided for the Director of Programmes position.

Official application form

Applicants should make sure they submit their materials before the stated deadline.

Application Deadline

20 September 2026

Because this is a time-limited vacancy, interested candidates should avoid waiting until the final day to prepare and submit their application.

What Makes LEAP Africa’s Workplace Different?

LEAP Africa’s description of its workplace combines professional responsibility with employee development and well-being.

The organisation’s approach can be summarised through several themes:

  • Purpose: Employees contribute to youth leadership and development.
  • Impact: The organisation seeks to create lasting transformation across communities.
  • Flexibility: Its hybrid structure provides physical and remote working options.
  • Development: Learning sessions, an L&D fund, and expert series support staff development.
  • Well-being: Leave, wellness initiatives, and organisational breaks are part of the employee experience.
  • Collaboration: Teamwork and knowledge sharing are strongly emphasised.
  • Growth: Employees are encouraged to take responsibility, accept challenges, contribute ideas, and shape their professional future.

Why the Director of Programmes Role Could Be Significant

For a professional seeking a senior role in the development sector, the Director of Programmes position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of strategy, programme implementation, leadership development, and social impact.

The position is not presented simply as an administrative programme-management role. LEAP Africa is looking for someone who can lead the design, delivery, and growth of its programmes while connecting those programmes to the organisation’s future strategic priorities.

This means the opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals who want to influence how development programmes are designed and implemented rather than simply supporting individual programme activities.

About Life as a LEAPer

LEAP Africa describes its workplace as people-first, emphasising the importance of creating an environment where employees can achieve meaningful work while also experiencing professional and personal fulfilment.

The organisation says employees are given room to:

  • Introduce new ideas
  • Take initiative
  • Contribute their talents
  • Accept responsibility
  • Take on challenging work
  • Develop their potential
  • Help shape their professional future

The organisation also emphasises that employees can contribute regardless of how long they have been with the organisation, suggesting an environment where ideas and initiative are encouraged.

Final Thoughts

The LEAP Africa Director of Programmes position offers an opportunity for an experienced and visionary professional to contribute to the design, delivery, and growth of programmes supporting youth leadership development and sustainable transformation across Africa.

With the position based in Lagos, Nigeria, the full-time role could be particularly relevant to professionals with strong programme leadership experience who are interested in contributing to an organisation focused on developing the next generation of African leaders.

Beyond the current vacancy, LEAP Africa also maintains a talent network through which interested professionals can receive updates about future vacancies and initiatives.

The most important date for applicants to remember is the 20 September 2026 application deadline. Interested candidates should review the official application information carefully and submit their application before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 is inviting motivated young people from across Europe to participate in an international learning and networking event focused on strengthening rural youth organisations, developing sustainable youth networks, and increasing the participation of rural communities in decision-making.

Organised by Rural Youth Europe (RYE) and the Rural Youth Parliament in Slovakia (VPMS), the SUSTAIN Seminar will take place from 8 to 13 November 2026 in Hokovce, Slovakia, with the main seminar programme running from 9 to 12 November.

The event will bring together 25 young people from across Europe for peer learning, organisational development, policy engagement, networking and practical planning. The activity forms part of the Rural Youth Forward project, which is co-funded by the Erasmus+ Programme of the European Union.

SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 Overview

The SUSTAIN Seminar is designed for young people who are actively involved in rural communities, youth organisations, youth work, farming, community initiatives or networks and who want to learn how to make such organisations more resilient, representative and influential.

Participants will examine the challenges faced by rural youth organisations and explore practical approaches to:

  • Strengthen organisational structures.
  • Improve leadership and governance.
  • Engage and retain volunteers.
  • Develop sustainable financing models.
  • Build partnerships.
  • Improve communication.
  • Encourage generational renewal.
  • Increase youth participation in policy-making.
  • Connect grassroots concerns with national and European decision-making processes.

The seminar will use a highly participatory approach, allowing participants to learn from one another while developing practical solutions that can be applied in their own communities and organisations.

What Is the SUSTAIN Seminar?

The SUSTAIN Seminar is an international seminar focused on sustaining and growing local and national rural youth organisations and networks and strengthening their European dimension.

Rural youth organisations play an important role in creating opportunities for young people to participate in their communities and make their voices heard in decision-making. However, many organisations face challenges such as dependence on short-term funding, limited volunteer capacity, informal organisational structures and difficulties transferring knowledge between generations.

The SUSTAIN Seminar seeks to address these challenges by helping participants understand what is required not only to establish rural youth organisations, but also to maintain and grow them over the long term.

The event will bring together 25 selected participants for several days of peer learning, organisational reflection and practical policy work.

About the Rural Youth Forward Project

The SUSTAIN Seminar is organised within the Rural Youth Forward project, which aims to cultivate resilient rural youth networks capable of contributing to more inclusive and participatory policy-making.

The project recognises that young people in rural areas need meaningful opportunities to influence decisions affecting their communities.

Through activities such as research, study visits, mentoring and seminars, the project seeks to strengthen the ability of rural youth organisations to:

  • Represent the interests of rural young people.
  • Develop sustainable organisational structures.
  • Participate in policy processes.
  • Build stronger networks.
  • Create meaningful opportunities for youth participation.
  • Contribute to local, national and European policy discussions.

What Will Participants Learn?

The SUSTAIN Seminar has been designed around practical organisational and policy challenges.

Participants will explore several important areas.

1. Organisational Sustainability

Participants will examine what makes a rural youth organisation healthy, resilient and capable of operating effectively over time.

Areas of discussion will include:

  • Organisational vision.
  • Governance.
  • Membership.
  • Programmes and services.
  • Feedback mechanisms.
  • Risk management.
  • Knowledge transfer.
  • Organisational development.

The aim is to help participants identify strengths and weaknesses within their own organisations or initiatives and develop practical approaches for improvement.

2. Leadership and Volunteer Engagement

Strong leadership is essential to maintaining youth organisations, particularly where organisations depend heavily on volunteers.

The seminar will explore sustainable approaches to:

  • Leadership development.
  • Volunteer engagement.
  • Generational renewal.
  • Knowledge sharing.
  • Organisational growth.
  • Building stronger teams.

Participants will have opportunities to exchange experiences and learn from the approaches used by other rural youth organisations across Europe.

3. Financing and Partnerships

Financial sustainability is another important issue for rural youth organisations.

Participants will examine approaches to:

  • Sustainable financing.
  • Partnership development.
  • Organisational growth.
  • Communication.
  • Building relationships with relevant stakeholders.

The seminar will encourage participants to think beyond short-term project funding and consider how organisations can develop stronger and more sustainable foundations.

4. European Union Youth Participation Tools

Participants will also learn about and explore European participation mechanisms that can help rural young people engage in policy-making.

These include:

  • Have Your Say.
  • The European Citizens’ Initiative.
  • Citizens’ panels.
  • Public consultations.
  • Petitions to the European Parliament.

These tools can provide avenues through which young people can move from identifying challenges in their communities to contributing to wider policy discussions.

5. Civic Dialogue

The programme will include a Civic Dialogue with European and national stakeholders.

The dialogue will be supported by Europe Direct and an invited Team Europe expert.

This component will give participants an opportunity to engage directly with stakeholders and better understand how youth perspectives can be brought into policy discussions.

6. European Parliament Simulation

Participants will take part in a simulation of the European Parliament.

Through this activity, participants will experience elements of policy negotiation and collaborative decision-making while working toward a shared Rural Youth Resolution.

This provides a practical way to understand how different perspectives can be brought together to develop common policy positions.

7. Organisational Action Plans

The seminar will not focus only on discussion and theory.

Participants will work on practical organisational action plans and recommendations that can contribute to the final policy paper of the Rural Youth Forward project.

This means participants will have the opportunity to translate what they learn during the seminar into concrete ideas and actions for their organisations and communities.

Learning Approach

The SUSTAIN Seminar will use an interactive and participatory learning model.

Rather than relying solely on traditional presentations, the programme will combine several learning methods, including:

  • Short expert inputs.
  • Peer-to-peer exchange.
  • Case studies.
  • Organisational self-assessment.
  • Workshop stations.
  • Civic Dialogue.
  • Policy simulation.
  • Collaborative drafting.
  • Group discussions.
  • Practical organisational planning.

Participants will therefore be expected to actively contribute their own experiences, knowledge, ideas and perspectives.

Key Project Resources

Participants will work with two important outputs from the Rural Youth Forward project:

Recommendations to Support Meaningful Youth Participation in Rural Areas

This resource provides recommendations intended to strengthen meaningful participation by young people in rural communities.

Quality Standards for Piloting and Mentorship Systems

Participants will also work with quality standards developed around piloting and mentorship systems.

During the seminar, participants will examine these resources in relation to their own organisational realities and explore how they can be transformed into practical next steps.

Who Can Apply?

The SUSTAIN Seminar is aimed at young people who have a connection to rural communities and rural youth development.

The organisers are particularly interested in applicants who fall into one or more of the following categories:

  • Active members of Rural Youth Europe member organisations or partner organisations.
  • Rural young people involved in local groups or community initiatives.
  • Young farmers.
  • Young people involved in emerging rural organisations.
  • Members of national rural youth networks.
  • Youth workers.
  • Youth leaders.
  • Youth practitioners.
  • People supporting rural youth through NGOs.
  • People involved in informal youth groups.
  • Individuals working with public institutions supporting rural youth.

Applicants may have experience or an interest in:

  • Youth work.
  • Education.
  • Rural development.
  • Youth participation.
  • Organisational sustainability.
  • Policy-making.
  • Community development.

Age Requirement

Applicants should be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of the seminar.

SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 Dates

The event will take place according to the following schedule:

  • Arrival: 8 November 2026
  • Main seminar programme: 9–12 November 2026
  • Departure: 13 November 2026
  • Overall dates, including travel: 8–13 November 2026

Location

The seminar will take place in:

Hokovce, Slovakia

Hokovce will serve as the setting for the international gathering of rural youth representatives, youth workers, leaders and practitioners from across Europe.

Travel, Accommodation and Meals

The organisers will provide substantial support for selected participants.

Accommodation

Shared accommodation will be covered by the organisers.

Meals

All meals will be covered from dinner on 8 November through breakfast on 13 November 2026.

Travel Reimbursement

Travel to and from Hokovce will be reimbursed in accordance with the project’s travel guidelines.

Further information regarding travel arrangements and accommodation will be provided to selected participants.

Participation Fee

There is no participation fee for the SUSTAIN Seminar.

Applicants should nevertheless wait until their participation has been officially confirmed before making travel or other arrangements.

How to Apply for the SUSTAIN Seminar 2026

Interested applicants must complete the official application form.

                                                            APPLY HERE

Application deadline: 25 September 2026.

Participation is by selection only, meaning that completing the application does not automatically guarantee a place at the seminar.

Selected applicants will receive a confirmation email following the selection process.

Applicants are specifically advised not to make travel arrangements or other commitments until their participation has been confirmed.

Application Deadline

The deadline is:

25 September 2026

Applicants should ensure that their application is completed and submitted before the deadline.

Because participation is competitive and limited to only 25 participants, interested applicants are encouraged to prepare their applications early rather than waiting until the final day.

Important Information for Applicants

Before applying, prospective participants should make sure that they can satisfy the main participation requirements.

Applicants should be prepared to:

  1. Demonstrate a connection to rural communities.
  2. Show an interest or experience in rural youth work, community development, youth participation, organisational development or policy-making.
  3. Participate in the entire programme from 8–13 November 2026.
  4. Communicate and participate actively in English.
  5. Share relevant experiences, practices or perspectives with other participants.
  6. Demonstrate motivation to apply what they learn after the seminar.
  7. Wait for official confirmation before making travel arrangements.

Why This Seminar Matters for Rural Youth

Rural young people often face challenges related to access to opportunities, participation in decision-making, organisational resources and representation.

Youth organisations can help address these challenges by creating structures through which young people can organise, communicate their concerns and participate in community and policy processes.

However, simply creating an organisation is not enough. Organisations need sustainable leadership, effective governance, committed volunteers, reliable partnerships and mechanisms for transferring knowledge between generations.

The SUSTAIN Seminar therefore focuses on the longer-term question of how rural youth organisations can remain effective, representative and influential.

By bringing together participants from different European countries, the seminar also creates an environment in which young people can compare experiences and identify solutions that may be adapted to their own local contexts.

Networking and International Exposure

One of the important aspects of the SUSTAIN Seminar is the opportunity to meet other young people working on rural youth issues across Europe.

Participants can exchange experiences with:

  • Rural youth leaders.
  • Young farmers.
  • Youth workers.
  • Community activists.
  • NGO representatives.
  • Youth practitioners.
  • Members of rural youth networks.

This international environment can encourage new partnerships, ideas and approaches to rural youth development.

Practical Outcomes for Participants

The seminar is designed to produce practical results rather than only providing theoretical knowledge.

Participants will have opportunities to develop:

  • Organisational action plans.
  • Recommendations.
  • Policy ideas.
  • New approaches to youth participation.
  • Strategies for organisational sustainability.
  • Ideas for volunteer engagement.
  • Approaches to partnership development.
  • Knowledge of European participation mechanisms.

Participants are also encouraged to use their learning and networks to support concrete actions after the seminar.

Organisers

The SUSTAIN Seminar is organised by:

  • Rural Youth Europe (RYE)
  • Rural Youth Parliament in Slovakia (VPMS)

The activity forms part of the Rural Youth Forward project and is co-funded by the European Union through EACEA under the Erasmus+ programme.

Important Disclaimer

The activity is part of the Rural Youth Forward project, co-funded by the European Union through EACEA. The views and opinions expressed by the organisers and participants are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union or EACEA. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Conclusion

The SUSTAIN Seminar 2026 in Hokovce, Slovakia offers a valuable opportunity for young people involved in rural communities and youth development to strengthen their organisational, leadership and policy-making skills.

With 25 participants from across Europe, the seminar will combine peer learning, practical workshops, organisational assessment, policy engagement, Civic Dialogue and a European Parliament simulation. Participants will also have the opportunity to develop practical action plans and contribute to recommendations for strengthening rural youth organisations.

The organisers will cover shared accommodation and meals, while travel will be reimbursed according to the project’s travel guidelines. There is also no participation fee, making the opportunity accessible to eligible young people who are committed to rural youth development.

Those interested should ensure they meet the age, country, rural-community connection, English-language and participation requirements and submit their application by the 25 September 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship is an exciting funding opportunity for documentary filmmakers who want to tell compelling, cinematic stories about the rapidly evolving world of psychedelics.

The fellowship is designed to support filmmakers producing documentaries that explore the science, policy, business and culture surrounding psychedelics. Through substantial production funding, the program seeks to help a new generation of filmmakers bring important and underreported stories to audiences through film.

For 2026, the fellowship offers two different grant opportunities: a Feature-Length Documentary Grant providing up to $20,000 to selected filmmakers and a Short-Form Documentary Grant providing up to $10,000 to selected filmmakers.

The application deadline is October 5, 2026.

The fellowship is a project of the U.C. Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics and is intended to foster a diverse group of filmmakers documenting a field that is undergoing significant scientific, cultural, political and social change.

About the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship

The psychedelic field is developing rapidly, with growing public interest in areas such as psychedelic-assisted therapy, scientific research, drug policy, cultural practices, business and emerging approaches to mental health and wellness.

The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship seeks filmmakers capable of transforming these developments into strong cinematic narratives.

Rather than simply funding general filmmaking activities, the fellowship is interested in projects with compelling stories that can engage audiences while providing deeper insight into the issues surrounding psychedelics.

According to the fellowship, it is looking for groundbreaking narratives fit for cinematic storytelling, particularly untold stories that can illuminate the science, policy, business and culture of this emerging era.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to filmmakers who have identified an important story that has not yet received sufficient attention.

What Funding Is Available?

The fellowship has two distinct funding tracks.

1. Feature-Length Documentary Grant

The Feature-Length Documentary Grant will provide:

  • Up to $20,000 per filmmaker
  • Three documentary filmmakers will be selected
  • Funding can support the production or post-production of a feature-length documentary
  • The documentary must be more than 40 minutes in length
  • The project should be a documentary or nonfiction film rather than fiction.

The feature-length grant is particularly suited to filmmakers who already have a substantial documentary project underway and need additional resources to complete production or post-production.

The application materials indicate that applicants should be the director of the project, have relevant prior work samples, have access to participants and locations, and be independently producing the project.

What can the funding help with?

Depending on the project’s needs, documentary production funding can potentially help a filmmaker cover costs associated with completing the project, such as:

  • Production activities
  • Post-production
  • Filming
  • Editing
  • Other legitimate project-related costs
  • Costs necessary to move the documentary toward completion

The fellowship does not require grantees to submit individual expenses for reimbursement. However, successful applicants are expected to provide a report explaining how the grant was spent and what was accomplished on the project.

2. Short-Form Documentary Grant

The Short-Form Documentary Grant will provide:

  • Up to $10,000 per filmmaker
  • Up to five documentary filmmakers may be selected
  • Funding is intended for the production of short-form documentaries
  • The film must be 40 minutes or less

This track is particularly important for emerging filmmakers because it can provide meaningful financial support for a shorter documentary project.

The fellowship specifically encourages student filmmakers currently enrolled in graduate programs to consider the Short-Form Documentary Grant, although additional eligibility requirements apply to student applicants.

Special Opportunity for Student Filmmakers

Students should pay particular attention to the eligibility requirements because the fellowship does not treat student applications in the same way as applications from established independent filmmakers.

For the student route, eligible applicants must be enrolled in a U.S.-based undergraduate or graduate-level film or journalism program at an intermediate level or higher and must have a faculty advisor supporting the project. The faculty advisor must provide a letter of support by the application deadline.

The fellowship’s FAQ further clarifies that only graduate-school-level student films are eligible for the Short-Form Documentary Grant.

Therefore, prospective student applicants should carefully check the current application requirements before preparing their submission.

Important student restriction

A current student cannot apply for the Feature-Length Documentary Grant under the current rules.

Who Can Apply?

One of the most attractive aspects of this opportunity is its international eligibility.

The fellowship confirms that both grants are open to filmmakers worldwide, regardless of nationality or citizenship status.

This means filmmakers from:

  • Africa
  • Asia
  • Europe
  • North America
  • South America
  • Central America
  • The Caribbean
  • Oceania
  • Other parts of the world

may apply, provided they satisfy the relevant grant’s project and applicant requirements.

There is no stated nationality or citizenship restriction preventing international filmmakers from applying.

For example, a qualified documentary filmmaker based in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Uganda, Rwanda, India, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Brazil or another country can potentially apply.

However, being from an eligible country alone does not guarantee eligibility. Applicants must also meet the requirements for their chosen grant.

Eligibility Requirements for Documentary Filmmakers

For the feature-length production/post-production route, the application requirements indicate that applicants should satisfy several important criteria.

1. You must be the director

The applicant must be the director of the documentary project.

This is important because the funding is intended to support individual filmmakers who are directly responsible for the creative direction of the project.

2. You need relevant previous work

Applicants must have prior work samples in which they played a principal role, such as:

  • Director
  • Co-director
  • Producer
  • Co-producer

Therefore, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their filmmaking experience through previous work samples.

3. The project must be documentary or nonfiction

The project must be a:

  • Documentary
  • Nonfiction film
  • Hybrid documentary

The fellowship does not support fiction films.

4. Feature projects must meet the required length

For the feature-length grant, the project must be at least 40 minutes in length according to the application materials.

5. The project should already be in production or post-production

The feature production/post-production grant is designed for projects that have progressed beyond the earliest development stage.

The application recommends that applicants have at least 10% of their footage shot by the application date, although applicants should consult the current FAQ for clarification about project stages.

6. You must have access to the story

Applicants must have confirmed access to:

  • Participants
  • Locations

This is important because the selection committee wants to see that the proposed documentary is realistically achievable.

7. The project must be independently produced

The documentary must be independently produced.

Works produced as “work for hire” are not eligible for the relevant production/post-production grant.

8. Only individuals can apply

Applications must come from individual filmmakers.

Organizations such as:

  • Universities
  • Foundations
  • Nonprofit businesses
  • Other organizations

cannot apply on behalf of a project.

What Types of Stories Is the Fellowship Looking For?

The fellowship is intentionally broad in its thematic scope.

It is interested in documentary stories examining different dimensions of psychedelics, including:

Science

Projects may explore scientific research and the developing understanding of psychedelic substances and their effects.

Policy

Filmmakers can examine laws, regulations, drug policy and the changing political environment surrounding psychedelics.

Business

Stories can investigate the growing commercial ecosystem surrounding psychedelic research, services, companies and related industries.

Culture

Documentaries may examine how psychedelics intersect with culture, communities, traditions and changing social attitudes.

The fellowship is particularly interested in untold and compelling narratives rather than generic treatments of the topic.

A strong application should therefore demonstrate why the proposed story matters and why audiences should care about it.

International Applicants Are Welcome

International filmmakers should take particular note of this opportunity.

The official FAQ explicitly states that filmmakers residing outside the United States can apply, and that both grants are open worldwide regardless of nationality or citizenship status.

Therefore, you do not have to be a U.S. citizen to apply.

However, international applicants should be aware that receiving fellowship funds may have tax implications, particularly for foreign nationals working in the United States. UC Berkeley may require documentation through its tax compliance process, and foreign nationals receiving fellowship payments may be subject to withholding depending on their circumstances.

Can the Documentary Be in Another Language?

Yes.

A filmmaker can produce a documentary in a language other than English, provided that the finished film will have English subtitles.

However, the application itself must be written in English because the selection committee does not have the capacity to evaluate applications in other languages.

This is particularly useful for filmmakers documenting psychedelic-related stories within communities where English is not the primary language.

Important Restrictions Applicants Should Know

Before applying, filmmakers should carefully consider several restrictions.

Fiction films are not eligible

The fellowship does not fund fiction films. The proposed project must be documentary, nonfiction or an eligible hybrid documentary.

Cannabis stories are not eligible

The fellowship’s FAQ states that it does not fund stories about cannabis and directs applicants to its definition of what qualifies as a psychedelic substance.

First-person illegal-substance experiences are not eligible

Applicants should not pitch stories centered on personally taking illegal substances and reporting on the experience. The fellowship specifically states that such stories cannot be supported for legal reasons.

Previously publicly distributed films are not eligible

A project that has already been publicly distributed is not eligible. This includes previous:

  • Theatrical screenings
  • Festival screenings
  • Educational screenings
  • Community screenings

Applicants should therefore ensure that the project they submit has not already been publicly distributed in these ways.

You cannot submit multiple stories

Each applicant may submit only one story pitch.

You cannot apply to both grant categories

Applicants must choose between the Feature-Length Documentary Grant and the Short-Form Documentary Grant.

You cannot apply to both grants during the same year.

Can Filmmakers Apply as a Team?

Yes, filmmakers can work with collaborators, co-directors or colleagues.

However, the fellowship requires one primary applicant to submit the application.

If awarded, the funds will be distributed to the primary applicant, who can then distribute funds to other members of the filmmaking team as appropriate.

This means a collaborative project does not necessarily have to be completed by one person, but the application needs to identify a primary applicant.

What Happens If You Are Selected?

Grant recipients have several responsibilities after receiving funding.

Successful fellows are expected to:

  1. Attend 3–4 virtual cohort meetings.
  2. Submit a written report within six months of the initial grant issuance.
  3. Explain how the grant money was spent.
  4. Describe what has been accomplished on the documentary.
  5. Share the finished film with the Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics once it is completed.
  6. Credit the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship in the finished film.

Student filmmakers also have additional expectations relating to completion of their film as part of their graduate-level coursework and faculty-advisor supervision.

How Will the Grant Money Be Paid?

The payment structure differs between the two grants.

Feature-Length Documentary Grant

Feature-length awardees receive:

  • Half of the award upfront
  • The remaining half six months later, after completing a project-update memo.

Short-Form Documentary Grant

Short-form awardees receive:

  • The full grant amount upfront.

The fellowship does not require recipients to submit individual expenses for reimbursement, although a six-month report explaining spending and project progress is required.

Is There an Application Fee?

No.

The application is free to submit.

This makes the opportunity particularly accessible to emerging filmmakers who may not have substantial resources available for application fees.

What Should Applicants Prepare?

A strong application should be built around a compelling documentary idea and demonstrate that the filmmaker has the experience, access and ability to execute it.

Applicants should be prepared to provide information about areas such as:

  • The documentary’s working title
  • Project stage
  • Story concept
  • Topic and context
  • Filmmaker background
  • Previous work
  • Artistic approach
  • Connection to the story
  • Access to participants and locations
  • Funding received so far
  • Project budget
  • Production plans

The application materials also ask filmmakers to explain the creative and narrative direction of their projects.

For student applicants, the application includes areas such as a logline, topic summary, story or concept summary, filmmaker statement, artistic approach, connection and access, and funding to date.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Although no application can guarantee funding, filmmakers can strengthen their submissions by paying close attention to the fellowship’s priorities.

1. Lead with the story

Do not make the application simply a discussion about psychedelics.

Instead, identify the human story at the center of the documentary.

Explain who the audience will follow, what is at stake and why the story is important now.

2. Demonstrate cinematic potential

The fellowship specifically seeks narratives suitable for cinematic storytelling.

Explain what viewers will see, hear and experience.

3. Show that you have access

If your documentary depends on specific people, communities, locations or institutions, explain how you will access them.

4. Demonstrate your filmmaking ability

Previous work samples are important, particularly for applicants seeking the feature-length funding.

Choose work that demonstrates your ability to tell compelling nonfiction stories.

5. Make the project’s relevance clear

Explain why the story matters within the larger conversation around psychedelics.

Consider the scientific, cultural, political, economic or social implications of the story.

6. Be realistic about production

A compelling concept needs a credible execution plan.

Make sure your proposed budget and production strategy are realistic.

7. Follow the eligibility rules carefully

Do not submit a project that falls into one of the excluded categories, such as fiction, cannabis-focused stories or previously publicly distributed films.

8. Remember the language requirement

If your film will be produced in another language, plan for English subtitles and prepare the application in English.

Important Information for Applicants Working With Collaborators

If several people are developing the documentary together, applicants should decide who will serve as the primary applicant before submission.

The fellowship does not split the application into multiple primary applicants. One person should submit the application and receive the funds, with the primary applicant then able to distribute funds to other team members.

Can You Reapply?

Yes.

Applicants who are unsuccessful may reapply if their project has undergone significant new developments since the previous application.

If reapplying, filmmakers should clearly explain what has changed or progressed since their earlier submission.

When Will Applicants Hear Back?

According to the current FAQ, applicants will be notified of award decisions by December 2026.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship is:

October 5, 2026

Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline because the fellowship states that extensions cannot be provided.

Apply Here

Feature-Length Documentary Grant:
Apply for the Feature-Length Documentary Grant HERE

Short-Form Documentary Grant:

Apply for the Short-form Documentary Grant HERE

Quick Summary of the Opportunity

Feature Details
Opportunity Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship
Category Grant / Fellowship
Host U.C. Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics
Feature-Length Grant Up to $20,000
Number of Feature Grants 3
Short-Form Grant Up to $10,000
Number of Short-Form Grants Up to 5
Feature Length More than 40 minutes
Short Form 40 minutes or less
Eligible Applicants Individual documentary filmmakers
International Applicants Yes
Nationality Restriction None stated; worldwide eligibility
Student Applicants Eligible under specific requirements, particularly for short-form
Application Fee None
Application Deadline October 5, 2026
Decision Notification By December 2026
Application Online

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly valuable for:

  • Independent documentary filmmakers
  • Nonfiction filmmakers
  • Documentary directors
  • Documentary producers who meet the primary-applicant requirements
  • Filmmakers researching the science of psychedelics
  • Filmmakers examining psychedelic policy
  • Filmmakers investigating the psychedelic business landscape
  • Filmmakers exploring the cultural dimensions of psychedelics
  • Filmmakers with compelling underreported stories
  • Graduate student filmmakers meeting the specific student requirements
  • International filmmakers from any country who satisfy the applicable eligibility requirements

The fellowship could be especially attractive to filmmakers who already have access to a compelling story and need financial support to take the project into production or complete post-production.

Learn more about this opportunity HERE

Conclusion

The Mycoskie–UC Berkeley Psychedelic Documentary Fellowship presents a significant funding opportunity for documentary filmmakers interested in exploring one of the world’s rapidly developing and increasingly debated fields.

With up to $20,000 available for feature-length documentaries and up to $10,000 for short-form documentaries, the program can provide valuable financial support for filmmakers seeking to transform important psychedelic-related stories into compelling cinematic work.

The fellowship is also notable for its worldwide eligibility, allowing qualified filmmakers to apply regardless of nationality or citizenship. At the same time, applicants must carefully distinguish between the two funding tracks, as the eligibility requirements differ, particularly for students.

For filmmakers with an original, well-developed and visually compelling documentary story about the science, policy, business or culture of psychedelics, this could be an opportunity worth serious consideration.

Deadline: October 5, 2026. Applicants should review the official requirements carefully and submit their application through the appropriate grant portal before the deadline.
