The Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) Early Career Conference Grants 2026–27 provide financial support for emerging researchers and academics who want to attend and actively participate in academic conferences in Commonwealth countries outside their country of work.

For early career academics, conferences can be an important part of building a successful research and teaching career. They provide opportunities to present research to an international audience, learn about new developments in a field, exchange ideas with other researchers, establish professional connections and bring new knowledge back to their universities.

Through the Early Career Conference Grants, the ACU is offering seven grants of up to GBP 2,000 each to eligible early career researchers and academics at ACU member universities.

The funding can contribute towards major costs associated with conference participation, including conference registration, international travel, accommodation, visa expenses and travel and health insurance.

Applications for the 2026–27 round open on 18 August 2026 and close on 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC.

Overview of the ACU Early Career Conference Grants

The Early Career Conference Grants are designed to help emerging academics gain valuable international conference experience.

Attending an academic conference is more than simply travelling to an event. For researchers who are still establishing themselves in their academic careers, a conference can provide an opportunity to:

  • Present research findings to other academics and specialists.
  • Receive feedback on research ideas and findings.
  • Discover the latest developments in their area of research.
  • Develop international professional networks.
  • Identify potential research collaborators.
  • Learn from established academics and researchers.
  • Exchange knowledge and ideas with colleagues from other institutions.
  • Strengthen their academic profile.
  • Bring new knowledge and perspectives back to their home university.
  • Improve teaching and research through exposure to current developments in their discipline.

The ACU states that conference participation can have a significant impact on both emerging academics and the universities that employ them.

What Is the Association of Commonwealth Universities?

The Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) is an international network of universities across the Commonwealth. Its programmes and funding opportunities support collaboration, professional development, research and knowledge exchange among universities and academics.

The Early Career Conference Grants form part of this broader effort to support emerging researchers and enable academic communities to benefit from international exchange.

What Funding Is Available?

For the 2026–27 funding round, seven grants are available, with each grant providing a maximum of:

GBP 2,000 per awardee

The grant can be used to help cover eligible expenses connected with attending and participating in the proposed conference.

Eligible costs include:

  1. Conference registration feeFunding can contribute towards the cost of registering for the conference.
  2. FlightsThe grant can be used towards flight costs associated with travelling to the conference.
  3. AccommodationAwardees can use the funding to help cover accommodation expenses during the conference trip.
  4. Visa costsWhere a visa is required for travel to the conference country, visa expenses can be covered by the grant.
  5. Travel and health insuranceFunding can also contribute towards travel and health insurance associated with the conference trip.

Applicants should carefully review the official application guidance and FAQs for further information about eligible expenses and funding conditions before submitting an application.

Who Can Apply for the Early Career Conference Grant?

The grant is specifically intended for early career researchers and academics at ACU member universities.

Applicants must satisfy the eligibility requirements established for the programme.

1. Applicants must be early career researchers or academics

An applicant must be an early career researcher or academic working at an ACU member university.

For the purposes of this grant, early career researchers and academics are generally defined as those who are within seven years of the start of their academic research or teaching career.

This means that applicants should consider when they began their academic research or teaching career when determining whether they fall within the seven-year early career period.

2. Career breaks may be considered

The seven-year criterion does not necessarily exclude applicants who have experienced a career break.

The ACU recognises that researchers and academics may take time away from employment for personal or professional reasons.

Examples of career breaks can include periods away from employment to:

  • Care for children.
  • Address personal circumstances.
  • Take time away from academic employment for professional reasons.
  • Deal with other circumstances that result in a temporary period away from employment.

Applicants who have experienced a career break should review the official guidance to determine how their circumstances affect their eligibility.

Applicants Must Identify a Suitable Conference

Applicants must identify a conference that they would like to attend as part of their application.

The proposed conference must satisfy important requirements.

The conference must take place in a Commonwealth country

The conference must be held in a Commonwealth country.

In addition, the conference must take place outside the applicant’s country of work.

This requirement makes the grant particularly valuable for academics seeking international exposure and opportunities to engage with researchers in other Commonwealth countries.

Conference dates

The proposed conference must take place between:

February 2027 and January 2028

Applicants should therefore identify a suitable conference falling within this period before submitting their application.

Applicants Must Actively Participate in the Conference

Simply attending a conference is not sufficient for this grant.

Applicants must have an active role in the proposed conference.

They must be doing at least one of the following:

  • Chairing a session
  • Presenting a paper
  • Presenting a poster

This requirement means applicants should already have identified an appropriate opportunity to contribute academically to the conference.

Researchers should therefore consider conferences that are directly relevant to their research interests and where they can demonstrate an active contribution.

Why Conference Participation Matters for Early Career Researchers

Academic conferences can be particularly valuable during the early stages of a research career.

For researchers who are still developing their academic networks and professional reputation, presenting at an international conference can create opportunities that may not be available through their normal university environment.

Conference participation can help early career academics to:

Share research

Presenting a paper or poster allows researchers to communicate their findings to academics working in related areas.

The feedback received during conference discussions can also help researchers identify strengths, weaknesses and potential improvements in their research.

Learn about new developments

Academic disciplines continuously evolve. Conferences bring together researchers who are working on current issues and emerging areas of research.

Participation can therefore help early career researchers remain informed about developments in their field.

Build professional networks

Meeting academics from other universities and countries can help researchers establish professional relationships that may continue after the conference.

These connections can potentially lead to research collaboration, knowledge exchange and other academic opportunities.

Strengthen research and teaching

Knowledge acquired through conference participation can be shared with colleagues and students at the researcher’s home university.

The benefits of the grant can therefore extend beyond the individual awardee and contribute to the wider academic community.

Important Ineligibility Conditions

Although the grant is intended to support international conference participation, there are important restrictions that applicants must understand.

Applicants must not have previously travelled outside their region of employment for work purposes

Applicants cannot have previously travelled outside their region of employment for work purposes, including conferences, since the start of their academic career.

This is an important eligibility requirement.

Applicants who have already travelled internationally for work or conference purposes during their academic career should carefully check the ACU’s definition of the relevant employment region and the application guidance before applying.

Previous ACU grant recipients cannot apply

Applicants who have previously received an ACU Early Career Conference Grant are not eligible to receive another award under this programme.

The programme was previously known as the Early Career Academic Grants, so previous recipients of the earlier version of the grant are also excluded.

Application Requirements

Before applying, prospective applicants should ensure they have identified an appropriate conference and understand the programme requirements.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate that:

  • They are an early career researcher or academic.
  • They work at an ACU member university.
  • Their academic career falls within the applicable seven-year period, taking eligible career breaks into consideration.
  • They have identified a suitable conference.
  • The conference is taking place in a Commonwealth country.
  • The conference is outside their country of work.
  • The conference will take place between February 2027 and January 2028.
  • They will actively participate by chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster.
  • They meet the ACU’s requirements concerning previous international work travel.
  • They have not previously received an ACU Early Career Conference Grant or its previous Early Career Academic Grant equivalent.

How to Apply for the ACU Early Career Conference Grant

Applications are submitted online through the ACU application system.

APPLY HERE

Applicants can also visit the official website HERE

Applicants should first review the official application guidance and frequently asked questions before completing the application.

 

Applicants with an existing MyACU account

If you already have a MyACU account, you can access the application form through the ACU’s online grant application system.

Applicants without a MyACU account

Applicants who do not already have a MyACU account must first register for an account.

After registering, applicants should follow the instructions contained in the registration email to log into the system and access the application form.

Applicants should ensure that they provide accurate information and carefully follow the application instructions.

Application Timeline

The application period for the 2026–27 Early Career Conference Grants is:

Applications open: 18 August 2026

Applications close: 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC

Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparing early rather than waiting until the final day.

This is particularly important because applicants need to identify an appropriate conference and demonstrate that they will actively participate through a presentation, poster or session chairing role.

Conference Period

The conference proposed in the application must take place between:

February 2027 and January 2028

Applicants should therefore look for conferences whose dates fall within this specified period.

Grant Conditions After Selection

Successful applicants will have responsibilities after receiving the grant.

All awardees are required to complete a report after completion of their award.

This reporting requirement means recipients should retain relevant information and documentation associated with their funded conference participation and be prepared to report on their experience and use of the award.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although meeting the eligibility criteria is essential, applicants can also take practical steps to make their applications clear and well prepared.

1. Choose a conference closely connected to your research

Select a conference that is directly relevant to your research or academic work.

A strong connection between your research and the conference can help demonstrate why participation would be valuable.

2. Confirm your participation role

Do not select a conference simply because it is interesting.

The programme requires applicants to actively participate by:

  • Chairing a session;
  • Presenting a paper; or
  • Presenting a poster.

Applicants should therefore have a clear understanding of their intended role.

3. Check the conference location

Confirm that the conference is being held in a Commonwealth country outside your country of work.

This is one of the central requirements of the grant.

4. Check the conference dates

Make sure the conference takes place between February 2027 and January 2028.

5. Confirm your university’s ACU membership

Before investing significant time in the application, verify that your university is an ACU member university.

6. Review the eligibility restrictions carefully

Applicants should pay particular attention to the rules concerning previous international work-related travel and previous receipt of an ACU Early Career Conference Grant.

7. Prepare early

Because applications close at a specific UTC time, applicants should avoid submitting at the last minute.

Early preparation also gives applicants time to review their information, confirm conference details and resolve any account or application issues.

Benefits of the Early Career Conference Grant

The ACU Early Career Conference Grant can provide several important benefits to emerging academics.

Financial support

The grant provides up to GBP 2,000, helping reduce the financial barriers associated with international conference participation.

International academic exposure

Participating in a conference in another Commonwealth country can expose researchers to different academic communities, approaches and research perspectives.

Research presentation experience

Applicants can gain experience presenting their research through papers or posters or by chairing academic sessions.

Professional networking

International conferences provide opportunities to meet academics, researchers and potential collaborators from different institutions.

Knowledge exchange

Awardees can bring knowledge gained at the conference back to their universities and share it with colleagues and students.

Career development

Conference participation can contribute to the professional development of early career researchers by increasing their exposure to the wider academic community.

Important Dates at a Glance

Item Details
Grant ACU Early Career Conference Grants
Number of grants 7
Maximum funding GBP 2,000 per grant
Applications open 18 August 2026
Application deadline 13 October 2026
Closing time 15:00 UTC
Eligible conference period February 2027 – January 2028
Conference location Commonwealth country outside country of work
Required participation Chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster
Post-award requirement Completion of an award report

Final Thoughts

The ACU Early Career Conference Grants 2026–27 represent a valuable opportunity for emerging researchers and academics to gain international conference experience without having to personally cover all of the associated travel and participation costs.

With seven grants of up to GBP 2,000, successful applicants can receive financial support for conference registration, flights, accommodation, visa expenses, and travel and health insurance.

More importantly, the programme can help early career academics share their research, learn about developments in their disciplines, establish professional networks and bring new knowledge back to their universities.

However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The applicant must be an early career researcher or academic at an ACU member university, the conference must be in a Commonwealth country outside the applicant’s country of work, and the applicant must actively participate by chairing a session, presenting a paper or presenting a poster.

Applicants should also check the restrictions relating to previous international work-related travel and previous receipt of an ACU Early Career Conference Grant.

With applications closing on 13 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC, eligible researchers should begin preparing their conference plans and application well in advance of the deadline.

Are you an experienced communications, journalism, health policy, science communication, community engagement, or digital audience development professional interested in using evidence to reach wider public audiences?

AcademyHealth is seeking a Civic Science Fellow, Evidence & Creator Partnerships to lead an innovative 18-month initiative focused on connecting health policy research and evidence with social media creators, community communicators, and other trusted messengers.

The fellowship, hosted by AcademyHealth, will focus on understanding how evidence can reach new and diverse audiences through creator partnerships, social media platforms, community networks, and civic dialogue.

The successful candidate will lead an initiative titled “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy.” The project will seek to develop an Evidence Creator Pipeline connecting health policy research with social media creators and community communicators who influence civic conversations and reach millions of people.

The fellowship is scheduled to run from September 2026 through March 2028 and offers a stipend of $85,000 per year. The position also includes paid leave, although health insurance and other benefits are not provided as part of the fellowship position.

About the AcademyHealth Civic Science Fellowship

AcademyHealth describes itself as the professional home and leading national organisation for health services researchers, policymakers, healthcare practitioners, and other stakeholders.

Its work focuses on improving understanding of methods and data used in health services research, strengthening professional skills, supporting the use of evidence in policy and practice, and advocating for evidence-based improvements in health and healthcare.

The organisation says it has also become a leading nonpartisan national voice on scientific integrity, federal data access, and the role of evidence in public debate. It emphasises an inclusive and equitable working environment and seeks to transform the field toward higher-impact and more equitable research.

The Civic Science Fellow will become part of this environment while leading a major project at the intersection of:

  • Health policy
  • Evidence and research
  • Science communication
  • Social media
  • Creator partnerships
  • Community engagement
  • Audience development
  • Civic dialogue
  • Digital communications
  • Public-interest communication

What Is the Evidence & Creator Partnerships Fellowship?

The Civic Science Fellow will lead an 18-month initiative designed to explore how evidence-based health policy information can reach audiences beyond traditional academic, scientific, and health policy institutions.

The initiative recognises that social media creators, community communicators, journalists, and other trusted messengers can play an important role in shaping how people encounter and interpret information.

Rather than relying solely on traditional methods of communicating research, the project will investigate how organisations can develop relationships with creators and community communicators who already have established audiences and trusted relationships.

The Fellow will therefore combine:

  1. Landscape research
  2. Relationship building
  3. Audience and network analysis
  4. Creator recruitment
  5. Partnership development
  6. Content experimentation
  7. Communications strategy
  8. Knowledge sharing
  9. Toolkit development
  10. Sustainability planning

The ultimate goal is to understand who can effectively carry evidence into new audiences, what makes creator partnerships successful, and how organisations can build sustainable networks of trusted evidence creators.

About the “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy” Initiative

The central project is titled “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy.”

The initiative will build an Evidence Creator Pipeline that connects health policy research with social media creators, community communicators, and other trusted messengers.

The project will pay particular attention to audiences that may not traditionally engage with scientific, academic, or health policy organisations.

This includes an interest in:

  • Cross-partisan audiences
  • Nontraditional audiences
  • Diverse communities
  • Social media audiences
  • Community networks
  • Trusted messengers
  • Alternative routes through which evidence can reach the public

The Fellow will not simply conduct research and produce a report. They will also apply the findings through live AcademyHealth communications and engagement initiatives.

This means the position combines research with practical experimentation.

The Fellow will use AcademyHealth’s organisational priorities as opportunities to test different approaches, learn from the results, and refine the Evidence Creator model.

Key Responsibilities of the Civic Science Fellow

The successful Fellow will have significant responsibility for designing and implementing the project.

1. Conduct a Landscape Assessment

The Fellow will lead a landscape assessment of social media creators and community communicators working at the intersection of:

  • Health
  • Policy
  • Evidence

The assessment will include a survey and rapid network analysis.

The purpose will be to understand factors such as:

  • What drives trust among audiences
  • How different audiences interact with information
  • Audience dynamics
  • Preferred partnership models
  • The characteristics of potential evidence creators
  • How evidence moves through different networks

2. Identify and Recruit Evidence Creators

The Fellow will develop and execute a strategy for identifying and recruiting a cohort of 5 to 10 emerging evidence creators.

The cohort is expected to represent diverse:

  • Backgrounds
  • Platforms
  • Communities
  • Audiences
  • Experiences

The goal is to identify creators who can potentially help communicate evidence to audiences that may not normally engage with traditional health policy or scientific institutions.

3. Develop Creator Partnership Models

The Fellow will pilot different partnership approaches with the selected creators.

These partnerships may involve:

  • Compensation
  • Skill-building
  • Content co-creation
  • A combination of these approaches

Importantly, the partnership models will be co-designed with the creators themselves.

This means the Fellow will need strong relationship-building skills and the ability to understand the needs, interests, audiences, and working styles of potential partners.

4. Develop and Produce Pilot Content

The Fellow will oversee the development and production of pilot content pieces.

The content will be:

  • Co-created with members of the creator cohort.
  • Designed for public audiences.
  • Distributed across at least three platforms.

This responsibility makes the position particularly relevant to professionals with experience in social media, digital communications, content strategy, creator partnerships, audience development, or public-interest communications.

5. Develop a Publicly Available Toolkit

Another major responsibility will be creating protocols and a publicly available toolkit.

The toolkit will be designed so that other scientific societies can use it to develop similar evidence creator networks.

This means the Fellow will need to document what works, develop practical processes, and translate lessons from the project into resources that other organisations can apply.

6. Present Findings

The Fellow will present project findings at the AcademyHealth Annual Research Meeting.

They will also contribute to a final report intended for broad dissemination.

The ability to communicate findings clearly to professional and public audiences will therefore be important.

7. Develop a Sustainability Plan

The Fellow will develop a plan for sustaining the Evidence Creator Network beyond the fellowship period.

This responsibility involves thinking beyond the initial 18-month project and considering how the network, partnerships, and lessons developed during the fellowship can continue to have an impact.

8. Establish and Manage an Advisory Group

The Fellow will also establish and manage a project advisory group.

The advisory group will draw on:

  • AcademyHealth staff
  • AcademyHealth members
  • External experts
  • Professionals with expertise in network analysis
  • Experts in policy influence
  • Health communications specialists

The Fellow will therefore need to be comfortable coordinating multiple stakeholders and managing relationships across different professional areas.

Who Is AcademyHealth Looking For?

AcademyHealth is looking for an emerging leader who is comfortable working with complex and ambiguous challenges.

The ideal candidate should be able to take an idea from the concept stage through to implementation.

The organisation is seeking someone who can:

  • Work independently.
  • Build relationships with people from different backgrounds and areas of expertise.
  • Translate complex evidence into compelling ideas.
  • Communicate effectively with public audiences.
  • Understand how people encounter and interpret information.
  • Explore new approaches to connecting evidence with civic dialogue.
  • Develop innovative approaches to creator and community partnerships.
  • Manage a major project with multiple stakeholders.
  • Adapt as the initiative develops.

AcademyHealth also states that applicants do not need to meet every listed expectation in order to apply. The organisation welcomes applications from a broad range of candidates and values diverse perspectives, backgrounds, experiences, and skills.

Desired Qualifications

Applicants should carefully consider the qualifications outlined by AcademyHealth before applying.

Educational Qualification

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university is required.

A Master’s degree is preferred, although it is not listed as mandatory.

Professional Experience

Candidates should have approximately 3 to 5 years of substantive professional experience in one or more relevant fields.

These include:

  • Health communications
  • Science communications
  • Health policy
  • Journalism
  • Community engagement
  • Related fields

The position is therefore aimed at candidates with meaningful professional experience rather than applicants who are completely new to communications or public engagement.

Project Management Experience

Applicants should have demonstrated experience managing or leading a complex project involving multiple stakeholders and moving parts.

This is particularly important because the Fellow will be responsible for an 18-month initiative involving creators, researchers, policymakers, community organisations, AcademyHealth staff, members, and external experts.

Creator, Influencer or Partnership Strategy Experience

AcademyHealth is seeking candidates with experience developing or executing:

  • Influencer strategies
  • Creator strategies
  • Audience-development strategies
  • Partnership strategies

Experience with public-interest, scientific, health, or policy organisations is particularly relevant.

Social and Digital Platform Knowledge

Candidates should understand social and digital platforms as ecosystems for:

  • Audience development
  • Relationship building
  • Civic engagement
  • Community engagement
  • Content strategy
  • Audience growth
  • Creator partnerships

This means the opportunity may be particularly attractive to professionals with backgrounds in digital communications, social media strategy, content creation, journalism, communications, or audience development.

For more information, VISIT HERE.

Relationship-Building Skills

Applicants should be able to identify potential partners and establish credible, authentic, and productive relationships across different sectors and communities.

These relationships may involve:

  • Researchers
  • Policymakers
  • Community organisations
  • Content creators
  • Professional networks
  • External experts

Strong interpersonal and networking skills will therefore be essential.

Ability to Experiment and Adapt

The successful candidate should have experience experimenting with new communication or engagement approaches.

AcademyHealth is particularly interested in candidates who can use:

  • Audience insights
  • Partner feedback
  • Evidence
  • Project results

to refine and improve strategies.

Communication Skills

Highly developed written and oral communication skills are required.

The Fellow must be able to take complex or technical subject matter and transform it into:

  • Compelling narratives
  • Public-facing content
  • Engagement strategies
  • Accessible communications

This is an important component of the role because the project is specifically concerned with helping evidence reach non-specialist audiences.

Understanding Communities and Trust

Applicants should demonstrate curiosity about how different communities:

  • Form opinions
  • Establish trust
  • Encounter information
  • Engage with information
  • Respond to evidence

The ability to understand differences between communities and audiences will be important to the project’s focus on diverse and nontraditional audiences.

APPLY HERE.

Health Policy Knowledge

Knowledge of health policy issues is preferred.

It is therefore an advantage for candidates who have previous exposure to health policy, health services research, healthcare communications, or related subjects.

Self-Motivation and Project Management

The Fellow should be self-motivated and have strong project management abilities.

They will be expected to manage an evolving 18-month initiative with limited supervision.

This makes independence, organisation, prioritisation, adaptability, and initiative important qualities for the position.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to valuing diversity and contributing to inclusive working and learning environments.

AcademyHealth emphasises the importance of diversity within its organisational culture.

AcademyHealth Allows Flexibility in Candidate Backgrounds

One important aspect of the opportunity is that AcademyHealth says it remains flexible regarding the types and depth of training and experience that potential Fellows may bring.

The organisation indicates that it expects to work with the selected Fellow to refine the project scope according to the Fellow’s background and help ensure the project’s success.

This means candidates should not necessarily eliminate themselves from consideration simply because their professional experience does not match every single item in the desired qualifications list.

Fellowship Duration

The Civic Science Fellowship is an 18-month fellowship position.

The scheduled fellowship period is:

September 2026 – March 2028

This is a substantial professional fellowship rather than a short-term internship or brief mentorship programme.

The Fellow will be responsible for leading a major initiative while also participating in the broader Civic Science Fellows cohort.

Fellowship Time Commitment

The Fellow will spend approximately:

  • 75% of their time, equivalent to approximately 30 hours per week, working with AcademyHealth as the host organisation.
  • 25% of their time, approximately 10 hours per week, participating in shared learning and networking activities as part of the Fellows cohort.

The cohort activities include weekly virtual sessions and an in-person convening.

This structure means the fellowship combines direct project work with professional development, peer learning, and networking.

Weekly Fellows Labs

From September 2026 through September 2027, the Fellow will participate in weekly virtual Fellows Labs.

These sessions take place on:

Tuesdays, 12:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time

The sessions are designed to support:

  • Shared learning
  • Peer exchange
  • Professional development
  • Collaboration across the Fellows cohort

This component provides Fellows with opportunities to learn alongside other professionals participating in the Civic Science Fellows programme.

Fellowship Stipend

The Civic Science Fellows programme provides a stipend of:

$85,000 per year

The position also includes paid leave.

However, applicants should note that health insurance and other benefits are not provided as part of this fellowship position.

The stipend is described as being set by the Civic Science Fellows programme.

Work Location and Remote Work

AcademyHealth operates a hybrid work environment, with options for remote and office work.

Importantly, candidates do not need to be physically located in the Washington, DC area.

The organisation specifically encourages candidates who live outside the Washington, DC area to apply.

This makes the opportunity potentially accessible to professionals who are not based in Washington, DC.

However, applicants should carefully consider the programme’s required travel commitments before applying.

Travel Requirements

Some travel is required as part of the fellowship.

The source identifies required participation in:

  • The Civic Science Fellows and Partners Convening in February 2027.
  • The AcademyHealth Annual Research Meeting in Boston in 2027.

Travel costs associated with required fellowship activities are covered by the fellowship grant.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to participate in required in-person fellowship activities when necessary.

Equal Opportunity and Diversity

AcademyHealth states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The organisation says applicants and employees will receive equal opportunity regardless of factors including:

  • Sex
  • Race
  • Colour
  • Religion
  • National origin
  • Age
  • Marital status
  • Personal appearance
  • Sexual orientation
  • Family responsibilities
  • Disability
  • Matriculation
  • Political affiliation
  • Source of income
  • Place of business or residence

The organisation also states that diversity is an integral part of its organisational culture and that it seeks to maintain staff diversity at all levels.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for qualified professionals whose background aligns with the fellowship’s focus on evidence, health communications, science communications, public engagement, social media, creator partnerships, audience development, journalism, or related fields.

The source does not specify a particular nationality, race, country, or continent as an eligibility requirement.

Instead, AcademyHealth describes itself as an Equal Opportunity Employer and says it welcomes a broad range of candidates.

Candidates should therefore focus on demonstrating the required education, professional experience, communication abilities, project management skills, partnership experience, and interest in evidence-based civic engagement.

Is This a Fellowship?

Yes.

This opportunity is explicitly described by AcademyHealth as an 18-month fellowship position.

The fellowship runs from September 2026 to March 2028, provides an annual stipend of $85,000, includes paid leave, and combines project work with shared learning and networking activities.

It should therefore be categorised as a Fellowship, rather than a job, internship, scholarship, grant, competition, conference, or award.

Application Requirements

Qualified applicants are asked to submit:

  1. A resume
  2. A cover letter

Applications should be submitted to AcademyHealth Human Resources by email at:

jobs@academyhealth.org

The organisation states that its hiring process will be conducted virtually, with interviews taking place by phone or video.

Applicants can also visit the AcademyHealth website for additional information.

Is There an Application Deadline?

The provided opportunity announcement does not state a specific application deadline.

Therefore, prospective applicants should not assume a deadline that is not included in the announcement.

Because the fellowship is scheduled to begin in September 2026, interested candidates should review the official AcademyHealth opportunity information and contact the organisation if they require confirmation of the current application status or closing date.

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable

The Civic Science Fellow position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of several rapidly evolving areas.

These include:

  • Science communication
  • Health policy
  • Digital media
  • Social media
  • Creator partnerships
  • Public engagement
  • Community communications
  • Audience development
  • Evidence-based communication
  • Civic dialogue
  • Network building

The Fellow will not only conduct research but will also develop practical partnerships, test communication models, produce content, create a publicly available toolkit, present findings, and develop a sustainability strategy.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant for professionals interested in developing innovative approaches to communicating evidence to wider audiences.

Professional Development and Networking

Another significant component of the fellowship is participation in the wider Civic Science Fellows network.

The programme brings together professionals including:

  • Scientists
  • Scholars
  • Community leaders
  • Journalists
  • Educators
  • Media producers
  • Public-interest organisations
  • Funders

The broader Civic Science Fellows programme is designed to encourage collaboration between science, diverse communities, and civil society.

Fellows and host organisations work on new pilots, partnerships, knowledge, models, and approaches to civic science.

The programme therefore provides not only an opportunity to lead an individual project but also to become part of a wider network of people working to strengthen connections between science, technology, innovation, communities, and civil society.

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity: Civic Science Fellow, Evidence & Creator Partnerships

Host organisation: AcademyHealth

Fellowship programme: Civic Science Fellows

Project: “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy”

Duration: 18 months

Fellowship period: September 2026 – March 2028

Stipend: $85,000 per year

Paid leave: Yes

Health insurance: Not provided

Work arrangement: Hybrid, with remote and office options

Washington, DC location required: No

Travel: Required for certain fellowship activities

Required travel: Civic Science Fellows and Partners Convening in February 2027 and AcademyHealth Annual Research Meeting in Boston in 2027

Education: Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred

Professional experience: 3–5 years of substantive relevant experience

Application materials: Resume and cover letter

Application method: Email Human Resources at jobs@academyhealth.org

Application deadline: Not specified in the provided announcement

Recommended Applicant Profile

A strong candidate for this fellowship would ideally be someone who combines professional communications experience with an interest in evidence, public engagement, digital platforms, and relationship building.

For example, a candidate may have experience in:

  • Health communications
  • Science communications
  • Journalism
  • Digital communications
  • Social media
  • Community engagement
  • Public policy communications
  • Audience development
  • Creator partnerships
  • Influencer partnerships
  • Content strategy
  • Public-interest communications

However, applicants should not assume that they need to come from one specific professional background. AcademyHealth states that it remains flexible regarding the types and depth of training and experience candidates may bring.

Tips for Preparing an Application

Although the announcement does not provide a specific application essay or additional questionnaire, applicants can strengthen their resume and cover letter by clearly demonstrating how their experience relates to the fellowship.

A strong application should make it easy for the selection team to identify evidence of:

Project Leadership

Highlight substantial projects you have managed or led, especially projects involving multiple stakeholders, deadlines, platforms, or deliverables.

Digital and Social Media Experience

If you have worked with social media platforms, content strategy, digital campaigns, audience development, creator partnerships, or online communities, make those experiences clear.

Communications Skills

Show examples of how you have taken complicated information and communicated it in a way that ordinary audiences can understand.

Partnership Development

Highlight examples of building relationships with creators, organisations, researchers, policymakers, communities, media professionals, or other stakeholders.

Innovation

Demonstrate situations where you tested a new communication or engagement approach, evaluated the results, and changed your strategy based on feedback or evidence.

Audience Understanding

Explain any experience you have in understanding audiences, analysing engagement, building communities, or developing content for specific groups.

Relevant Health or Policy Knowledge

If you have experience in health policy, healthcare, health research, science communication, public policy, or a related area, make sure it is clearly visible in your application.

Final Thoughts

The Civic Science Fellow, Evidence & Creator Partnerships opportunity at AcademyHealth is an 18-month professional fellowship focused on an increasingly important challenge: finding effective ways to connect research and evidence with wider public audiences.

Through the “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy” initiative, the successful Fellow will research creator and community networks, recruit 5–10 emerging evidence creators, develop partnership models, oversee content creation across multiple platforms, build a publicly available toolkit, present findings, and develop a sustainability plan for the Evidence Creator Network.

The fellowship offers a $85,000 annual stipend, paid leave, remote and hybrid working options, professional development through the Civic Science Fellows cohort, and opportunities to participate in significant research and communications activities.

It is particularly suited to professionals with approximately 3–5 years of experience in areas such as health communications, science communications, journalism, health policy, community engagement, digital communications, creator partnerships, audience development, or related fields.

Importantly, the announcement does not identify a specific nationality, race, country, or continent as a requirement for eligibility. AcademyHealth states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes applications from a broad range of candidates.

The provided announcement does not include an application deadline. Interested applicants should therefore review the official AcademyHealth opportunity information and submit the required resume and cover letter to jobs@academyhealth.org while confirming the current application status.

item.content:encoded:
The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is inviting qualified candidates to apply for its Procurement Intern position in Accra, Ghana. The opportunity provides professional exposure to procurement operations within a Pan-African economic policy organisation and involves supporting procurement activities across institutional and donor-funded projects.

The position is based in Accra and is expected to run from the time of appointment through 31 December 2026. ACET is seeking a candidate with a relevant Bachelor’s degree and practical procurement experience who can support purchasing, tendering, supplier management, contract administration, procurement planning, compliance, record keeping, and stakeholder coordination.

ACET Procurement Intern Opportunity 2026

The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is a Pan-African economic policy institute focused on supporting Africa’s long-term economic growth through transformation.

The organisation works directly with African governments, businesses, and civil society across countries and borders to help remove policy barriers to sustainable and inclusive development.

ACET is headquartered in Accra, Ghana, while maintaining a diverse workforce across several continents. The organisation describes itself as African-led and globally connected, drawing on the expertise of its staff and partners to conduct research, provide policy advice, and amplify Africa’s voice through events, advocacy, and engagement.

The Procurement Intern will join ACET’s procurement function and work under the supervision of the Procurement Specialist.

Position Details

Details Information
Organisation African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET)
Position Procurement Intern
Location Accra, Ghana
Reporting to Procurement Specialist
Duration Immediate through 31 December 2026
Posted 1 September 2026
Application deadline 11 September 2026
Application documents CV and Cover Letter

The position is specifically designed to support ACET’s procurement function across institutional and donor-funded activities.

What Does the ACET Procurement Intern Do?

The Procurement Intern will support the day-to-day delivery of procurement activities.

Working under the Procurement Specialist, the successful candidate will coordinate assigned procurement processes, maintain procurement records and systems, support tendering and evaluation, assist with contract administration, and ensure procurement activities comply with ACET policies, applicable donor requirements, and established procedures.

The role requires strong organisation, attention to detail, integrity, responsiveness, and the ability to complete assigned procurement responsibilities within established procedures and delegated authority.

Procurement Operations and Support Responsibilities

A major part of the role will involve supporting routine procurement operations.

The Procurement Intern will be responsible for activities such as:

  • Receiving and processing procurement requests.
  • Confirming that required documentation is complete before procurement begins.
  • Preparing purchase orders and work orders for goods and non-consulting services.
  • Processing documents through the required approval channels.
  • Coordinating supplier and bidder invitations.
  • Receiving and maintaining the safe custody of bids and proposals.
  • Maintaining procurement records.
  • Supporting the identification and sourcing of qualified suppliers and service providers.
  • Working with user departments to ensure procurement requirements and specifications are properly addressed.
  • Preparing solicitation and tender documents using approved ACET templates.
  • Monitoring procurement timelines.
  • Following up with suppliers, user departments, and other stakeholders regarding outstanding actions.
  • Providing internal requesters with timely updates about the progress of procurement activities.

These responsibilities mean that the successful candidate will need to be highly organised and comfortable working with documents, suppliers, internal departments, deadlines, and established procurement procedures.

Tendering, Evaluation and Award Support

The Procurement Intern will also support ACET’s tendering and evaluation processes.

Responsibilities include:

  • Coordinating pre-bid or pre-proposal meetings where applicable.
  • Supporting clarification processes.
  • Assisting with bid or proposal opening sessions where applicable.
  • Providing administrative and procedural support to evaluation panels.
  • Preparing evaluation materials.
  • Preparing minutes and other records required during evaluations.
  • Checking evaluation documentation for completeness and consistency.
  • Submitting relevant documentation to the Procurement Specialist for review.
  • Preparing draft award and notification documents.
  • Preparing notifications for successful and unsuccessful bidders as directed.

This part of the role provides exposure to the procurement cycle beyond purchasing, including tender preparation, evaluation administration, award documentation, and communication with bidders.

Contract Administration Responsibilities

Contract administration is another important component of the position.

The Procurement Intern will assist with:

  • Preparing draft contracts.
  • Preparing purchase orders and agreements.
  • Using approved templates for procurement documentation.
  • Maintaining and updating the contract register.
  • Recording contract values.
  • Tracking key contract dates.
  • Monitoring deliverables and milestones.
  • Recording renewal dates.
  • Monitoring assigned contracts.
  • Following up on supplier and consultant deliverables.
  • Following up on routine performance issues.
  • Preparing draft contract extensions, amendments, and variations for review.
  • Supporting contract close-out.
  • Ensuring that required documentation, deliverables, and acceptance records are completed.

This means candidates interested in developing experience in procurement and contract management could gain exposure to several stages of the contract lifecycle.

Procurement Planning, Monitoring and Reporting

The successful candidate will also support procurement planning and reporting activities.

This includes:

  1. Supporting the Procurement Specialist in preparing and updating annual procurement plans.
  2. Supporting project procurement plans.
  3. Maintaining procurement trackers.
  4. Monitoring assigned procurement activities.
  5. Identifying procurement delays and outstanding actions.
  6. Reporting delays promptly to the Procurement Specialist.
  7. Assisting with procurement activity reports.
  8. Supporting donor procurement reports.
  9. Compiling documentation required for audits.
  10. Organising records required for reviews and management reporting.

These duties require candidates to have strong record-keeping and organisational skills and the ability to monitor several activities at the same time.

Compliance, Integrity and Procurement Records

Procurement requires strict adherence to procedures, transparency, and accountability.

The Procurement Intern will therefore support compliance by:

  • Ensuring assigned procurement activities follow ACET procedures.
  • Ensuring applicable donor requirements are followed.
  • Maintaining complete and auditable procurement files.
  • Supporting screening of bidders, suppliers, and consultants against applicable sanctions and debarment lists before awards.
  • Administering conflict-of-interest declarations for evaluation panel members.
  • Maintaining relevant conflict-of-interest records.
  • Maintaining supplier files and contract documentation.
  • Following ACET’s record-retention requirements.
  • Uploading and updating procurement documents on InSoft and applicable donor procurement or project-tracking systems.
  • Promptly reporting suspected fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, conflicts of interest, or other procurement irregularities to the Procurement Specialist.

Integrity is therefore a particularly important aspect of the position.

APPLY HERE.

Stakeholder Support and Communication

The Procurement Intern will interact with internal departments as well as external suppliers and service providers.

The role includes:

  • Providing professional procurement support to user departments.
  • Supporting project teams.
  • Assisting internal stakeholders.
  • Providing procedural guidance under the direction of the Procurement Specialist.
  • Reviewing draft Terms of Reference and specifications for completeness.
  • Identifying gaps in procurement documentation.
  • Communicating with bidders, suppliers, and consultants on routine procurement matters.
  • Providing accurate information within authorised parameters.
  • Supporting responses to procurement-related queries from internal and external stakeholders.

Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills will therefore be useful for applicants.

Other Procurement Duties

In addition to the core responsibilities, the Procurement Intern may also:

  • Support basic market research.
  • Help identify potential suppliers.
  • Contribute information that can assist with procurement activities and cost estimates.
  • Improve procurement records and templates.
  • Contribute to procurement trackers.
  • Support improvements to administrative processes.
  • Provide procurement support to other organisational units during periods of increased workload.
  • Perform other procurement-related duties assigned by the Procurement Specialist.

The position may therefore involve a combination of routine procurement administration, research, documentation, stakeholder communication, and process improvement.

ACET Procurement Intern Qualifications

ACET has specified both educational and professional experience requirements for the position.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must have a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas:

  • Procurement and Supply Chain Management
  • Business Administration
  • Law
  • Quantity Surveying
  • A related discipline

A relevant professional or postgraduate qualification in procurement, supply chain management, business, law, or a related area will be an added advantage.

Professional Experience Requirements

Although the position is titled Procurement Intern, ACET’s terms of reference specify relevant professional experience requirements.

Candidates must meet one of the following three routes:

Route 1: Bachelor’s Degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management

Applicants may qualify with:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management; and
  • At least two years of relevant procurement experience following the Bachelor’s degree.

Route 2: Bachelor’s Degree in a Related Discipline

Applicants may qualify with:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline; and
  • At least three years of relevant procurement experience following the Bachelor’s degree.

Route 3: Master’s Degree

Applicants may qualify with:

  • A Master’s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field; and
  • At least one year of relevant procurement experience following the Master’s degree.

Applicants should carefully compare their qualifications and professional experience against these three routes before submitting an application.

Additional Experience That Would Be an Advantage

Experience in the following environments is listed as an advantage:

  • Donor-funded projects
  • Development organisations
  • NGOs
  • Similar environments

Experience working with procurement frameworks used by the World Bank, other multilateral development banks, bilateral donors, or comparable organisations is also an advantage.

Candidates with this type of experience may therefore be particularly well positioned for the role.

Skills and Abilities Required

ACET identifies five broad areas of knowledge, skills, and abilities for the position:

  • Procurement and contract administration
  • Organisation and delivery
  • Communication and stakeholder management
  • Systems and digital skills
  • Integrity and professionalism

These areas reflect the practical nature of the role.

A successful applicant should be able to manage procurement documentation carefully, communicate professionally with stakeholders, work with digital procurement systems, monitor activities and deadlines, and maintain high standards of integrity.

About ACET

The African Center for Economic Transformation is a Pan-African economic policy institute working to support long-term economic transformation in Africa.

ACET works with governments, businesses, and civil society to address policy barriers that affect sustainable and inclusive development.

The organisation is headquartered in Accra, Ghana, but has staff based across multiple continents. ACET describes itself as African-led and globally connected, using research, policy advice, events, advocacy, and engagement to contribute to economic transformation and improve livelihoods across Africa.

For more information about the organisation, CLICK HERE

ACET Values

The organisation operates around five core values:

Pioneering

ACET seeks to push boundaries in the spirit of being a “think and do” organisation.

Respect

The organisation believes that respecting one another helps people and the organisation grow.

Integrity

ACET emphasises transparency and accountability in its actions.

Collaboration

The organisation believes that its best results are achieved by working effectively together.

Excellence

ACET aspires to the highest level of critical thinking when addressing difficult problems.

Applicants should consider these values when preparing their applications, particularly their cover letters.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity at ACET

ACET states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to inclusion and diversity in the workplace.

The organisation says it has a zero-tolerance approach to discrimination and harassment and draws from a diversified Pan-African and global talent base.

ACET also states that recruitment, remuneration, and employee development are based on skills and suitability for the work performed.

Procurement Intern Application Deadline

The application deadline for the ACET Procurement Intern position is:

11 September 2026

The organisation states that applications must be received by 11 September 2026.

Because the deadline is close, interested applicants should prepare their application documents as soon as possible.

How to Apply for the ACET Procurement Intern Position

Interested candidates are required to submit:

  1. A CV
  2. A Cover Letter

The cover letter should explain why the applicant is the most suitable candidate for the Procurement Intern position.

Applications should be submitted through the application link provided by ACET.

Application portal: Apply for the ACET Procurement Intern position

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates the experience that ACET is seeking.

Relevant areas to highlight include:

  • Procurement experience
  • Supply chain management
  • Tendering and evaluation
  • Supplier sourcing
  • Contract administration
  • Purchase orders
  • Procurement planning
  • Procurement reporting
  • Donor-funded procurement
  • Procurement compliance
  • Record keeping
  • Stakeholder management
  • Digital procurement systems
  • Market research
  • Audit preparation

The cover letter should go beyond simply repeating the CV. It should explain how the applicant’s education, experience, skills, and professional interests align with the responsibilities of the position.

Applicants with experience involving donor procurement frameworks should make this particularly clear because ACET identifies donor-funded projects and knowledge of major donor procurement frameworks as advantages.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals with an academic background in:

  • Procurement and Supply Chain Management
  • Business Administration
  • Law
  • Quantity Surveying
  • Related disciplines

However, the candidate must also satisfy one of ACET’s specified professional experience pathways.

The position is therefore not limited to someone who has never worked before. Despite the title “Procurement Intern,” the published requirements specify one to three years of relevant procurement experience depending on the applicant’s academic qualification.

Is the ACET Procurement Intern Opportunity Open to Africans?

ACET describes itself as a Pan-African organisation and states that it draws from a diversified Pan-African and global talent base.

However, the vacancy information provided does not explicitly state that applicants must be African nationals or citizens of a particular African country.

The position is based in Accra, Ghana, and candidates should consider the location requirements when applying.

ACET also states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to inclusion and diversity.

Duration of the Procurement Internship

The position is listed as running:

Immediately through 31 December 2026.

This means the successful candidate is expected to begin as soon as possible following appointment and continue in the position through the end of December 2026.

Location

The Procurement Intern position is based in:

Accra, Ghana

The vacancy identifies Accra as both the organisation’s headquarters and the location of this particular role.

Applicants should therefore consider their ability to work in Accra when deciding whether to apply.

Important Details at a Glance

Organisation: African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET)

Position: Procurement Intern

Location: Accra, Ghana

Posted: 1 September 2026

Duration: Immediate through 31 December 2026

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Law, Quantity Surveying, or a related discipline

Experience: Two years after a Bachelor’s in Procurement and Supply Chain Management; three years after a Bachelor’s in a related discipline; or one year after a relevant Master’s degree

Preferred additional experience: Donor-funded projects, development organisations, NGOs, World Bank or comparable procurement frameworks

Application documents: CV and cover letter

Application deadline: 11 September 2026

Application method: Online application through the designated careers portal

Conclusion

The ACET Procurement Intern 2026 opportunity offers a professional procurement role within a Pan-African economic policy organisation headquartered in Accra, Ghana.

The successful candidate will support a broad range of procurement functions, including procurement requests, purchase orders, supplier sourcing, tendering, evaluation, contract administration, procurement planning, reporting, compliance, record management, and stakeholder communication.

The opportunity is particularly suited to candidates with a Bachelor’s or Master’s qualification in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Law, Quantity Surveying, or a related field, provided they meet one of ACET’s specified experience pathways.

Experience in donor-funded projects, NGOs, development organisations, and international procurement frameworks such as those used by the World Bank or comparable institutions can provide an additional advantage.

The role is based in Accra, Ghana, runs from immediately through 31 December 2026, and applications must be received by 11 September 2026.

Interested candidates should prepare a strong CV and a tailored cover letter explaining why they are suitable for the position and submit their application through the designated recruitment portal before the deadline.
