item.content:encoded:
The 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program is an opportunity for young leaders who have previously participated in the AFS Youth Assembly to take on a representative and leadership role within the global AFS Youth Assembly community.

The program is designed for young people who want to become pioneers in their communities, amplify youth voices on the global stage, promote youth participation in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and represent the mission and programs of the AFS Youth Assembly.

Ambassadors serve as official representatives of the AFS Youth Assembly for a one-year term. During this period, they are expected to promote Youth Assembly programs and initiatives, encourage other young people to participate, and nominate youth to become delegates.

Applications are currently open, and interested candidates must complete the application process before the stated deadline.

AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program 2027

The AFS Youth Assembly is a global platform focused on cultivating a network of young leaders and changemakers through exchange, education, action and impact.

The Ambassador Program builds on this mission by giving previous Youth Assembly delegates an opportunity to remain engaged with the organization and contribute to its wider youth leadership network.

According to the program, ambassadors are expected to become pioneers in their communities, help young people have a voice at the global level, and represent the mission of the AFS Youth Assembly.

Successful ambassadors serve as official representatives of the Youth Assembly and take part in activities that promote its programs and initiatives.

What Does an AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Do?

An ambassador serves for a one-year term and has an active role in promoting the AFS Youth Assembly.

The main responsibilities include:

  1. Representing the AFS Youth Assembly

    Ambassadors serve as official representatives and help communicate the organization’s mission, programs and opportunities to young people in their communities and networks.

  2. Promoting Youth Assembly Programs

    Ambassadors are responsible for disseminating information about AFS Youth Assembly programs and initiatives.

    This may involve communicating opportunities through personal networks, schools, universities, youth organizations and digital platforms.

  3. Nominating Young People

    Ambassadors are expected to nominate youth who may be interested in becoming delegates at the AFS Youth Assembly.

  4. Conducting Engagement Activities

    Ambassadors may promote and represent the Youth Assembly through activities such as:

    • Speaking at events
    • Participating in radio programs
    • Appearing on podcasts
    • Participating in television shows
    • Writing blogs
    • Creating social media posts
    • Conducting other engaging promotional activities

These activities provide ambassadors with opportunities to communicate with different audiences and encourage greater youth participation in the Youth Assembly.

Qualifications for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program

The Ambassador Program has several specific eligibility requirements.

Applicants should carefully review these requirements before submitting an application.

Previous AFS Youth Assembly Participation

Applicants must have attended the AFS Youth Assembly as a Delegate.

This is an important requirement because the Ambassador Program is specifically geared toward youth who have previously participated in the Youth Assembly.

Current Education or Organizational Affiliation

Applicants must either:

  • Be currently pursuing an undergraduate, graduate or postgraduate degree at a recognized academic institution during the present academic year; or
  • Be affiliated with or represent an organization with a mission similar to that of the AFS Youth Assembly.

This allows the program to consider both students and young people actively connected with relevant organizations.

Active Role in School or Community

Applicants should demonstrate that they have an active role within their school or community.

This may include participation in youth initiatives, community activities, leadership programs, organizations or other forms of civic engagement.

Knowledge and Experience With the Sustainable Development Goals

Applicants should have experience and knowledge in working on the Sustainable Development Goals.

The program is therefore particularly relevant to young people who have already engaged with global development, sustainability, community development or related initiatives.

Commitment to Youth Empowerment

Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to:

  • Youth empowerment
  • The Sustainable Development Goals
  • Giving young people greater opportunities to participate
  • Supporting youth voices and leadership

Self-Starter and Problem Solver

The program seeks candidates who are proactive and capable of identifying and addressing challenges independently.

Being a self-starter is important because ambassadors are expected to actively promote the Youth Assembly and carry out activities during their one-year term.

Social Media and Content Creation Skills

Applicants should be social media savvy and have experience creating content.

The program specifically identifies experience with formats such as:

  • Short videos
  • TikTok content
  • Social media posts
  • Other digital content

These skills are relevant because ambassadors will play a role in communicating Youth Assembly opportunities and initiatives through different platforms.

Communication and Coordination Skills

Excellent communication and coordination skills are also required.

Ambassadors may communicate with young people, organizations, event audiences, media platforms and the Youth Assembly team, making effective communication particularly important.

Fundraising and Sponsorship Experience

Experience in fundraising and sponsorship development is listed as a plus.

This means it is beneficial but is not presented as a mandatory qualification.

Candidates with experience developing partnerships, raising funds or securing sponsorships may therefore have an additional strength in their application.

Responsibilities and Standards for AFS Ambassadors

Being selected as an ambassador involves ongoing responsibilities throughout the one-year term.

Ambassadors are expected to complete their assigned activities and maintain appropriate standards when representing the Youth Assembly.

Reporting and Measuring Progress

Ambassadors must complete an online report and present their strategy and progress using:

  • Metrics
  • Photos
  • Specific activities conducted

This means successful ambassadors should be prepared to document their activities and demonstrate what they have accomplished during their term.

Completing Assignments

Ambassadors are expected to complete assignments fully and before the applicable deadlines.

Reliability and timely completion are therefore important elements of the ambassador role.

Using the Official Promotional Materials

Ambassadors must use the Youth Assembly’s communication promo kit and follow the relevant protocols when presenting information about Youth Assembly programs.

This helps ensure consistency and accuracy when ambassadors communicate publicly about the organization.

Providing Accurate Information

Ambassadors must always present accurate information about Youth Assembly programs.

This is particularly important when promoting opportunities to potential delegates and other young people.

Following the Code of Conduct

Ambassadors are expected to follow the organization’s code of conduct and uphold its stated values.

These include:

  • Professionalism
  • Integrity
  • Respect for Diversity
  • Friendship

Benefits of Becoming an AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador

The Ambassador Program provides several potential benefits for selected participants.

Certificate of Recognition

Ambassadors can receive a Certificate of Recognition for their dedication and work with the AFS Youth Assembly.

This provides formal recognition of their contribution during the ambassador term.

Potential Speaking Opportunities

Ambassadors may receive potential opportunities to speak at events.

These experiences can help young leaders strengthen their public speaking and communication skills.

Conference Fee Waivers

Ambassadors may receive complimentary AFS Youth Assembly conference fee waivers, subject to applicable conditions.

Delegate Discounts

Ambassadors may also receive discounts for delegates attending the AFS Youth Assembly, subject to conditions.

Professional Networking

The program provides opportunities to build a professional network.

Ambassadors can interact with other young leaders, Youth Assembly participants and individuals connected to the broader AFS network.

Professional Development

Ambassadors have opportunities to enhance their skills and professional development through their activities and engagement with the Youth Assembly.

Opportunities to Attend AFS Youth Assemblies

The program provides opportunities for ambassadors to attend AFS Youth Assemblies, subject to applicable conditions.

Youth Leadership Experience

Serving as an ambassador provides a leadership opportunity for young people who want to inspire and engage other youth around global challenges and the Sustainable Development Goals.

Opportunity to Publish Online

Ambassadors may have opportunities to publish content online as part of their engagement with the Youth Assembly.

Outstanding Ambassador Recognition

The program also provides additional recognition for ambassadors who perform their responsibilities with excellence.

Outstanding Ambassadors will receive Outstanding Ambassador recognition.

According to the program information, outstanding ambassadors will also receive special mention at the Youth Assembly and may be promoted through the Youth Assembly’s social media platforms.

Ambassador status and recognition are determined based on factors including:

  • Quality of work
  • Level of activity in promoting the Youth Assembly
  • Effectiveness of promotional activities
  • Completion of assigned tasks
  • Communication with the Youth Assembly team
  • Efforts to promote and support the Youth Assembly
  • Quality of Youth Assembly nominees submitted according to procedures
  • Overall delegation the ambassador will bring to the next Youth Assembly session

This means simply being selected as an ambassador does not automatically guarantee outstanding recognition. Performance throughout the ambassador term is an important factor.

How to Apply for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program

The application process consists of two steps.

Step 1: Written Application

Interested candidates must first complete and submit the application form for consideration.

Applicants should provide information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and have the experience, motivation and skills needed to serve as an ambassador.

Step 2: Online Interview

Shortlisted candidates will proceed to an online interview.

Only candidates who are shortlisted will receive an interview request from the AFS Youth Assembly staff.

If the interview is successful, selected candidates will receive further information and instructions.

First-Come, First-Serve Application Review

Applicants should pay particular attention to the way applications will be reviewed.

The program states that applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis.

The first 200 applications will be prioritized.

Applications submitted after the first 200 may be placed on a waitlist and reviewed as needed.

This makes early application particularly important. Candidates who meet the eligibility requirements should not necessarily wait until the deadline to submit their application.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program is September 18, 2026.

Applicants should submit their application before the deadline and, importantly, consider applying early because the first 200 applications are prioritized.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly suitable for previous AFS Youth Assembly delegates who are already active in their schools, universities, communities or youth organizations.

Strong candidates are likely to be young people who can demonstrate a combination of:

  • Previous AFS Youth Assembly participation
  • Youth leadership experience
  • Community engagement
  • SDG knowledge and experience
  • Commitment to youth empowerment
  • Communication skills
  • Social media experience
  • Content creation abilities
  • Organizational and coordination skills
  • Initiative and problem-solving ability
  • Interest in representing a global youth platform

Applicants with fundraising or sponsorship development experience may have an additional advantage because the program identifies this experience as a plus.

Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable for Young Leaders

The Ambassador Program can be particularly valuable for young people who want to build a stronger international leadership profile.

Rather than participating only as a delegate, ambassadors take on an ongoing responsibility to represent and promote the Youth Assembly.

This can provide experience in areas such as:

Leadership

Ambassadors are responsible for promoting programs, engaging other young people and representing the Youth Assembly.

Public Communication

Speaking at events and participating in media activities can help ambassadors develop their communication and public-speaking abilities.

Digital Communication

Social media and content creation experience can be strengthened through practical promotional activities.

Networking

Ambassadors can expand their professional and youth leadership networks.

SDG Engagement

The role provides an opportunity to remain actively engaged with the Sustainable Development Goals and youth-led development initiatives.

Community Impact

By nominating young people and promoting Youth Assembly programs, ambassadors can help create opportunities for other young people in their communities.

Tips for Potential Applicants

Candidates preparing their application should ensure that they can clearly demonstrate the requirements stated by the program.

Highlight Your Previous Youth Assembly Experience

Because previous participation as a Youth Assembly delegate is required, make this experience clear in your application.

Demonstrate Community Engagement

Explain your current role in your school, university, organization or community and provide concrete examples of activities you have undertaken.

Show Your SDG Experience

Do not simply state that you are interested in the SDGs. Demonstrate how you have worked on or contributed to SDG-related activities.

Highlight Your Digital Skills

If you have created social media campaigns, short videos, TikTok content, blogs or other digital materials, highlight this experience.

Demonstrate Initiative

Provide examples that show you can independently identify opportunities, solve problems and take action.

Emphasize Communication Skills

The ambassador role involves communicating with different audiences, so examples of public speaking, coordination, media engagement or community outreach can strengthen your application.

Apply Early

Because the first 200 applications are prioritized, submitting early is particularly important.

Conclusion

The 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program provides previous Youth Assembly delegates with an opportunity to move beyond participation and take on an active leadership and representation role.

Successful ambassadors serve for one year and help disseminate information about AFS Youth Assembly programs, nominate young people to become delegates, participate in promotional activities and represent the Youth Assembly within their communities and wider networks.

The program is particularly suited to young leaders who are active in their schools, communities or organizations, have experience with the Sustainable Development Goals, understand youth empowerment and possess strong communication and social media skills.

Selected ambassadors can benefit from recognition, networking, professional development, potential speaking opportunities, opportunities to attend Youth Assemblies, online publishing opportunities and other forms of engagement, subject to applicable conditions.

One of the most important points for prospective applicants is that applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, with the first 200 applications prioritized. Therefore, eligible previous AFS Youth Assembly delegates should consider submitting their application well before the September 18, 2026 deadline.

For young leaders who want to continue contributing to the AFS Youth Assembly community while developing their leadership, communication and professional networks, the Ambassador Program offers a meaningful way to represent and advance youth participation on a global platform.

item.content:encoded:
The Takemi Program in International Health at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is accepting applications for its 2027–2028 fellowship year, offering mid-career health professionals and researchers an opportunity to spend an academic year at Harvard developing an independent research project, strengthening their research capacity, and advancing their leadership in international health.

The program is particularly relevant to professionals working on health systems, global health, health policy, health financing, disease prevention and control, health equity, public health, and other challenges involving the mobilization and allocation of limited resources for better health outcomes.

Applications for the 2027–2028 program are currently open, and the official deadline is December 31, 2026, at midnight EST (USA).

About the Harvard Takemi Program in International Health

The Takemi Program in International Health is an interdisciplinary research and leadership program at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

The program brings a small group of mid-career health professionals and scholars to Harvard for an academic year to conduct focused research and develop their capacity for research and leadership.

The program’s central focus is on understanding how limited resources can be mobilized, allocated, and managed to improve health and health systems. Its research has a strong emphasis on practical health challenges, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

Since its establishment in 1983, the program has developed a large international network of Takemi Fellows. Harvard currently reports that more than 330 fellows from more than 60 countries have participated in the program.

The program was named after Dr. Taro Takemi, a distinguished Japanese physician-scientist who served as president of the Japan Medical Association for more than two decades.

What Is the Takemi Fellowship?

The Takemi Program is designed for mid-career researchers and health professionals who have already developed substantial professional and research experience and want to dedicate an academic year to advancing a specific research project.

Unlike a conventional degree program, the Takemi Program is centered on an individual research project.

Each fellow works with a Harvard faculty advisor and uses the fellowship year to:

  • Develop and conduct a focused research project
  • Analyze existing data
  • Strengthen research methodology
  • Engage with Harvard faculty and researchers
  • Participate in weekly academic seminars
  • Present research findings and receive feedback
  • Develop a publication-quality research paper
  • Strengthen leadership capacity
  • Build international professional networks
  • Explore relevant Harvard coursework and academic resources

The program is conducted in person in Boston and does not offer a remote fellowship option.

Who Is the Takemi Program Designed For?

The program is primarily intended for mid-career health professionals and researchers.

Applicants should not view this as a typical early-career fellowship or a postgraduate degree scholarship. Harvard specifically describes the program as being for professionals and researchers who already have an advanced degree, significant work and research experience, publications, and demonstrated leadership potential.

Potential applicants may come from areas such as:

  • Public health
  • Medicine
  • Pharmacy
  • Nursing
  • Epidemiology
  • Health economics
  • Health policy
  • Health systems
  • Global health
  • Health administration
  • Nutrition
  • Health financing
  • Disease prevention and control
  • Implementation science
  • Health services research
  • Social and behavioral sciences
  • Other fields relevant to international health

The most important consideration is not simply the applicant’s professional title. The proposed research should fit the program’s broader focus on improving health and health systems through better use of resources, stronger policies, and evidence-based interventions.

What Makes the Takemi Program Different?

The Takemi Program is particularly valuable because it provides fellows with something that can be difficult to obtain while working full-time: dedicated time and an academic environment to focus intensively on research.

Harvard describes the program as providing fellows with the space, time, and flexibility to enhance their research and leadership capacity.

Rather than requiring fellows to complete a conventional curriculum, the program allows them to concentrate on a research project that is relevant to their professional work and future contribution to health policy or practice.

This makes the program especially relevant for professionals who already have a research question, access to data, and a clear idea of how their research could contribute to improving health systems or policy.

Research Focus of the Takemi Program

The program’s research emphasis is broad but strongly connected to real-world international health challenges.

Research can examine questions related to:

Health Systems

Projects may investigate how health systems are organized, financed, managed, or improved.

Health Policy

Applicants may explore policies affecting health outcomes, healthcare delivery, access, equity, financing, or population health.

Health Resource Allocation

A central theme of the program is understanding how scarce resources can be allocated more effectively to achieve better health outcomes.

Disease Prevention and Control

Research may focus on strategies for preventing, controlling, or managing important diseases and health threats.

Health Promotion

Projects may examine interventions designed to improve population health and encourage healthier behaviors.

Global Health

The program is particularly interested in major health challenges affecting low- and middle-income countries and approaches that can produce practical improvements.

Health Equity

Research examining inequalities, access to healthcare, marginalized populations, and equitable distribution of health resources may also fit within the program’s broader research priorities.

Harvard states that Takemi research has a strong practical emphasis and that projects should be closely connected to action and to the fellow’s work after returning home.

A Critical Requirement: Your Data Must Already Be Available

One of the most important requirements for prospective applicants is that their research project must be ready for analysis before the fellowship begins.

Takemi does not support active data collection during the fellowship.

Harvard explicitly states that fellows are expected to conduct their research using data they bring with them and that having the necessary data collected before the program begins is mandatory.

This means applicants should not propose a research project that depends on spending the fellowship year conducting extensive surveys, recruiting participants, collecting laboratory samples, or otherwise gathering primary data.

Instead, a strong proposal should demonstrate that:

  1. The research question has already been defined.
  2. The necessary data are available.
  3. The applicant has access to the data.
  4. The data are sufficiently prepared for analysis.
  5. The proposed methodology can realistically be implemented during the fellowship year.
  6. The research can result in a publication-quality paper.

This requirement is particularly important when designing the research proposal.

Faculty Supervision and Research Mentorship

Each selected fellow is matched with a Harvard faculty advisor based on the fellow’s background and proposed research.

Applicants do not need to independently secure a Harvard faculty supervisor before applying.

Harvard explains that fellows are matched with faculty mentors after selection based on their background and proposed research.

The faculty advisor provides guidance and feedback throughout the research process.

Fellows also receive guidance from the Takemi Program leadership and benefit from interactions with other fellows and the broader Harvard community.

Weekly Takemi Seminar Series

An important component of the program is the weekly Takemi Seminar Series.

The seminars expose fellows to a broad range of research topics, methodologies, and perspectives through presentations by Harvard faculty and distinguished visiting scholars.

The seminars also create opportunities for discussion and intellectual exchange between fellows, faculty, and invited speakers.

This means the fellowship is not simply an individual research residency. Fellows become part of an academic community where they can receive feedback, exchange ideas, and learn from researchers working on different international health challenges.

Research Presentations During the Fellowship

Takemi Fellows are expected to present their research progress during the fellowship.

According to Harvard, fellows participate in:

  • Preliminary presentations
  • Mid-year presentations
  • Final presentations
  • Final academic poster presentation

These presentations provide opportunities for fellows to receive feedback from faculty advisors and peers as they develop their research.

By the end of the fellowship, fellows are expected to produce a final paper of publishable quality and a research poster.

Opportunity to Audit Harvard Courses

Although the Takemi Program is primarily a research fellowship, fellows may also have opportunities to audit classes at Harvard Chan School.

They are also encouraged to attend Harvard Chan seminars and other academic events.

This can allow fellows to supplement their research experience with additional academic exposure based on their professional and research interests.

Fellowship Duration

The Takemi Program is a full academic-year fellowship.

Harvard states that the fellowship runs from:

August 1 through June 30

Fellows are expected to arrive before the program orientation, which takes place in late August. The certificate ceremony is generally held in early May.

Applicants should therefore plan for a substantial period of residence in Boston rather than treating the fellowship as a short-term visiting researcher position.

What Applicants Need to Submit

The application includes several components designed to assess the applicant’s academic background, professional experience, research capacity, motivation, and leadership potential.

The application requires the following:

1. Eligibility Questionnaire

Applicants must complete the program’s eligibility questionnaire.

This helps establish whether the applicant meets the fundamental requirements for consideration.

2. Proof of English Language Proficiency

Applicants must provide evidence of English proficiency.

The application accepts:

  • TOEFL
  • IELTS

Applicants who attended a university where English was the language of instruction may submit a copy of their transcript as evidence, according to the application instructions provided.

3. Statement of Interest

The Statement of Interest is an important component of the application.

Applicants should explain:

  • Why they are interested in the Takemi Program
  • Why the fellowship is important at this stage of their career
  • How the program will contribute to their professional development
  • What they can contribute to the Takemi community
  • Why they believe they would succeed in the program
  • What they hope to gain from the fellowship
  • What they plan to do after completing the program

A strong statement should connect the applicant’s past experience, current research interests, Takemi fellowship objectives, and future professional plans.

4. Basic Information

Applicants will provide standard personal and application information through the online application portal.

5. Education and Professional Experience

Applicants must provide information about their academic and professional background.

This section allows the program to understand the applicant’s progression and experience in relation to the fellowship.

6. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must upload a current CV in PDF format.

The CV should clearly present relevant:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Professional experience
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Leadership roles
  • Awards and recognition
  • Relevant projects
  • Professional activities

Because the Takemi Program is designed for mid-career professionals, the CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s professional trajectory and research accomplishments.

7. Research Proposal

The research proposal is arguably one of the most important components of the application.

Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than five pages, excluding the title page and references.

The proposal should be:

  • Single-spaced
  • 12-point Times New Roman
  • Submitted as a PDF

The proposal should include the following sections.

Title Page

The title page should clearly identify the proposed research project.

Summary of the Proposed Project

The summary should provide a concise overview of the research, including:

  • The central research problem
  • Specific aims and objectives
  • Potential significance of the research

The application guidance suggests approximately half a page for this section.

Specific Aims

Applicants should clearly explain what the research intends to accomplish.

The suggested length is approximately half a page to one page.

Background and Significance

This section should establish:

  • What is already known
  • What problem remains
  • Why the problem matters
  • Why the proposed research is important
  • How the project contributes to existing knowledge

Data Sources

Applicants should identify the data that will be used.

This is particularly important because the program requires the necessary data to already be collected before the fellowship begins.

Research Design and Methods

This section should explain how the research will be conducted.

Applicants should clearly describe:

  • Research design
  • Analytical approach
  • Variables or measures
  • Methods
  • Data analysis
  • Any relevant methodological considerations

The application guidance suggests approximately two pages for this section.

References

The proposal should conclude with relevant references.

8. Publication List

Applicants must provide a list of their publications.

This requirement reflects the program’s emphasis on applicants who already have demonstrated research experience and scholarly output.

Applicants should ensure that the publication list is accurate, clearly organized, and consistent with the CV.

9. Published Document in English

Applicants must provide a document published in English.

This gives the selection committee an opportunity to assess the applicant’s ability to communicate scholarly work in English.

10. Three References

Applicants must provide the names and contact information of three referees.

After the application is submitted, referees receive an automated request to submit their references to the Takemi Program.

Applicants should therefore choose referees who can provide meaningful evidence of their:

  • Research ability
  • Professional experience
  • Leadership potential
  • Academic development
  • Contribution to health systems or policy
  • Capacity to benefit from the fellowship

Who Is Eligible for the Takemi Program?

Harvard’s current application guidance states that applicants should be mid-career researchers and professionals who have:

  • Completed an advanced degree
  • Significant work experience
  • Significant research experience
  • Publications in internationally recognized journals
  • Demonstrated potential for leadership in their home countries
  • Appropriate preparation to benefit from the program
  • Strong English-language ability

The program is primarily designed for people who are already established in their professional careers rather than recent graduates.

Is the Takemi Program Open to International Applicants?

Yes.

The Takemi Program is explicitly international and brings together professionals and researchers from around the world.

Harvard’s historical fellowship network includes fellows from countries across:

  • Africa
  • Asia
  • Europe
  • The Middle East
  • North America
  • South America
  • Other regions

Harvard describes the program as having a particular emphasis on fellows from low- and middle-income countries.

Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted to U.S. citizens or residents.

Professionals from eligible countries around the world can apply if they meet the program’s academic, professional, research, and leadership requirements.

Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement?

The program does not specify a racial or ethnic eligibility restriction.

Its emphasis is instead on professional background, research experience, leadership potential, English proficiency, and the relevance and quality of the proposed research.

Harvard also states that the Takemi Program welcomes research examining issues related to racism, discrimination, marginalization, structural inequality, and other related issues when relevant to international health research.

Preference for Low- and Middle-Income Countries

The Takemi Program has a longstanding commitment to strengthening research and leadership capacity among professionals from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

Harvard states that the program has historically focused on building the capacity of mid-career researchers from LMICs and that most Takemi Fellows have focused their work on LMIC-related challenges.

This makes the program particularly relevant for professionals whose work addresses health challenges in developing and emerging economies.

Financial Support and Funding

Applicants should pay close attention to funding arrangements.

The Takemi Program states that incoming fellows are generally responsible for securing funding to support their fellowship year. Boston is an expensive city, and Harvard encourages accepted candidates to plan carefully for the cost of living and other expenses.

However, limited funding mechanisms are available.

For example, Harvard reports that a contribution from the Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (JPMA) provides partial financial support for up to two fellows from low-income countries each year. Candidates can indicate their interest in this support during the application process.

Importantly, applicants should not assume that the Takemi fellowship automatically provides full funding for the entire year.

Accepted applicants may need to secure funding through other sources, such as:

  • Employer or professional development funding
  • Government funding
  • Research grants
  • International fellowships
  • Fulbright funding
  • Other external funding sources

Harvard provides information about potential external funding sources for incoming fellows.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the 2027–2028 Takemi Program in International Health is:

December 31, 2026

Applications must be submitted by midnight EST (USA) on December 31, 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the application includes multiple documents, a research proposal, English-language documentation, publications, and three references.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The Harvard Takemi Program in International Health 2027–2028 represents a significant opportunity for experienced health professionals and researchers seeking dedicated time to conduct high-quality research, strengthen their leadership capacity, and contribute to better health policies and systems.

The program is particularly relevant to mid-career professionals with advanced degrees, substantial research and professional experience, international publications, and demonstrated leadership potential. Its strong emphasis on practical research makes it especially suitable for applicants whose work addresses health challenges in low- and middle-income countries.

The program is also international rather than restricted to U.S. applicants, making it potentially relevant to qualified health professionals and researchers across Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, Europe, and other regions. Harvard’s fellowship network demonstrates its longstanding international reach.

The application deadline is December 31, 2026, at midnight EST (USA). Applicants should begin preparing well in advance because the application requires a research proposal, statement of interest, CV, publication list, English-language documentation, writing sample, and three references.

item.content:encoded:
NASA has opened applications for its Spring 2027 Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) Internship Program, offering students the opportunity to gain hands-on experience by contributing to real NASA projects and working alongside NASA professionals.

For students interested in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, space exploration, aeronautics, research, communications, business, and other fields relevant to NASA’s mission, the OSTEM program can provide valuable practical experience, professional development, and exposure to one of the world’s leading space and science organizations.

The application deadline for the Spring 2027 NASA OSTEM Internships is September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Applicants should therefore review available opportunities, confirm their eligibility, prepare their application materials, and submit their applications before the deadline.

About the NASA OSTEM Internship Program

NASA’s Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) runs internship opportunities designed to give students practical experience connected to NASA’s missions.

According to NASA, the OSTEM program provides students with short-term, hands-on opportunities to work on real NASA projects. Interns can develop technical and professional skills while receiving guidance and mentorship from NASA personnel.

NASA provides more than 2,000 students annually with opportunities through its OSTEM internship program.

The program is therefore more than a conventional academic internship. Selected students have the opportunity to gain experience in a professional environment and contribute to projects connected to NASA’s broader work in science, technology, aeronautics, and space exploration.

What Is the Spring 2027 NASA OSTEM Internship?

The Spring 2027 OSTEM internship is part of NASA’s annual internship cycle.

NASA operates three major OSTEM internship sessions each year:

  • Spring
  • Summer
  • Fall

For the Spring 2027 cycle, applications must be submitted by September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

The spring and fall OSTEM internships generally run for approximately 15 weeks, while summer internships generally last around 10 weeks.

What Do NASA OSTEM Interns Do?

NASA OSTEM interns work on projects that contribute to the agency’s mission.

Depending on the specific internship, responsibilities can vary considerably. NASA offers opportunities across a broad range of academic and professional disciplines.

Interns may have the opportunity to:

  • Work on real NASA projects
  • Conduct research and analysis
  • Support scientific or engineering activities
  • Develop technical solutions
  • Analyze data
  • Assist with communications and outreach
  • Contribute to technology development
  • Work with NASA scientists, engineers, researchers, and other professionals
  • Develop professional and workplace skills
  • Gain practical experience related to their academic field
  • Participate in a professional NASA work environment

Importantly, NASA states that its internship opportunities are not limited exclusively to STEM majors. NASA also offers opportunities for students from non-STEM disciplines, depending on the available projects and NASA’s workforce needs.

This means students should not automatically assume that they are ineligible simply because their degree is not in engineering, physics, computer science, or another traditional STEM discipline.

Key Benefits of a NASA OSTEM Internship

A NASA internship can provide several important benefits for students seeking to build their academic and professional careers.

1. Gain Hands-On Professional Experience

One of the major advantages of the OSTEM program is the opportunity to move beyond classroom learning.

Interns can work on projects and activities that provide practical experience and help them understand how their academic knowledge can be applied in a professional environment.

2. Work on Real NASA Projects

OSTEM internships are designed around actual NASA projects rather than purely theoretical assignments.

Students can contribute to work related to NASA’s broader mission in areas such as science, technology, aeronautics, and space exploration.

3. Learn From NASA Professionals

Interns have the opportunity to work with NASA experts and mentors.

This can expose students to professional approaches to:

  • Research
  • Problem-solving
  • Project management
  • Technical work
  • Communication
  • Collaboration
  • Innovation

4. Strengthen Your Resume

Having hands-on experience with NASA can be a valuable addition to a student’s academic and professional profile.

The experience can demonstrate exposure to:

  • Professional project environments
  • Research or technical work
  • Team collaboration
  • Problem-solving
  • Innovation
  • Mission-oriented work

Students can subsequently use the experience when applying for graduate programmes, scholarships, research opportunities, jobs, and other internships.

5. Develop Technical and Professional Skills

NASA describes OSTEM internships as opportunities to build both technical skills and career readiness.

Depending on the project, students may develop skills related to their discipline while also strengthening transferable skills such as communication, teamwork, organization, critical thinking, and professional problem-solving.

6. Explore Careers at NASA

An OSTEM internship can also help students understand what it is like to work within NASA and explore potential career paths.

For students interested in eventually pursuing careers in aerospace, science, engineering, research, technology, communications, administration, or other NASA-related fields, an internship can provide useful exposure to the organization.

Who Can Apply for the NASA OSTEM Internship?

NASA’s current eligibility requirements specify that OSTEM candidates must meet several requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be a U.S. citizen
  • Be at least 16 years old at the time of application
  • Have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale
  • Be a full-time or part-time college student, from undergraduate through graduate level
  • Be enrolled in a degree-granting programme at a U.S. Department of Education-accredited college or university
  • Be studying in a course of study aligned with NASA’s needs

NASA also indicates that educators who are enrolled as students can be eligible to apply.

Students who have recently graduated may also be eligible for internships taking place during the three internship sessions immediately following their graduation, subject to NASA’s eligibility requirements.

Do You Need to Study a STEM Subject?

Not necessarily.

The name “Office of STEM Engagement” might lead some applicants to believe that only STEM students can apply. However, NASA explicitly states that it offers internships for non-STEM majors as well.

The key consideration is whether the applicant’s academic programme and qualifications align with the requirements of the particular internship opportunity.

Therefore, students from fields outside traditional STEM disciplines should review the individual project descriptions rather than automatically ruling themselves out.

How Long Is the NASA OSTEM Internship?

The length of the internship depends on the session.

NASA’s current programme information indicates:

  • Spring: approximately 15 weeks
  • Summer: approximately 10 weeks
  • Fall: approximately 15 weeks

The exact dates and working arrangements can vary according to the specific internship project.

Is the NASA OSTEM Internship Paid?

Yes.

NASA describes OSTEM internships as paid internships.

This makes the opportunity particularly attractive to students who want to gain high-level professional experience while receiving financial compensation during the internship.

Applicants should review the specific opportunity listing for the details applicable to the position they are applying for.

Is the NASA Internship Available to International Students?

This is an important point for international applicants.

For the standard NASA OSTEM Internship Program, NASA’s current eligibility requirements state that applicants must be U.S. citizens.

Therefore, students living in countries such as Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, India, the United Kingdom, Canada, or other countries generally cannot apply for the standard Spring 2027 OSTEM internship solely on the basis of being international students.

NASA previously operated international internship arrangements through its International Internship (I²) programme. However, NASA’s current international internship page states that the International Internship (I²) programme is not being offered at this time.

Students who are not U.S. citizens should therefore carefully distinguish the standard OSTEM programme from any separate NASA international opportunities that may become available in the future.

Important Citizenship Requirement

The citizenship requirement is particularly important because some online posts about NASA internships may make the opportunity appear open to students worldwide.

For the current OSTEM programme, NASA explicitly states:

U.S. citizenship is required.

International students should not assume that studying at a U.S. university automatically makes them eligible for OSTEM. The official eligibility requirement is U.S. citizenship.

What Academic Level Is Eligible?

NASA’s OSTEM programme is intended for students at multiple levels of higher education.

Eligible students can include:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students
  • Other college-level students who meet NASA’s requirements

The programme requires applicants to be enrolled in an eligible degree-granting programme at a U.S.-accredited institution.

The minimum age is 16 years old at the time of application.

GPA Requirement

Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of:

3.0 out of 4.0

This is an important eligibility requirement and should be checked before submitting an application.

Applicants should also review the requirements listed on each individual internship opportunity because individual projects may have additional qualifications or preferences.

Application Deadline for NASA Spring 2027 Internships

The most important date for students interested in this opportunity is:

September 14, 2026

The official NASA internship page specifies that applications for the Spring 2027 OSTEM session close at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on September 14, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications.

Technical problems, incomplete information, missing documents, or last-minute application issues can create unnecessary risks.

How to Apply for the NASA Spring 2027 OSTEM Internship

Applicants should begin by reviewing the available NASA OSTEM internship opportunities and identifying projects that match their academic background, interests, skills, and career goals.

The general process is:

Step 1: Review the Available Opportunities

Look through the NASA OSTEM internship listings and identify projects that match your interests and qualifications.

Step 2: Check the Eligibility Requirements

Before spending significant time on an application, confirm that you meet the basic requirements, including:

  • U.S. citizenship
  • Minimum age
  • GPA
  • Student status
  • Educational institution requirements
  • Academic field requirements

Step 3: Identify the Best-Fit Projects

Do not simply apply randomly.

Review the project description and consider:

  • What skills are requested?
  • What academic background is preferred?
  • What responsibilities are involved?
  • What technical or professional experience would be useful?
  • How does the project relate to your career goals?

Step 4: Prepare Your Application

Make sure your application accurately communicates your:

  • Academic background
  • Relevant experience
  • Skills
  • Research interests
  • Career objectives
  • Relevant projects
  • Leadership or extracurricular activities

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Applications for Spring 2027 must be submitted by:

September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Applicants should allow sufficient time to complete and review their application before the deadline.

A Note for International Applicants

International students should pay particular attention to the citizenship requirement before investing time in an OSTEM application.

The current NASA OSTEM requirements state that candidates must be U.S. citizens.

NASA’s International Internship programme page also currently states that the International Internship (I²) programme is not being offered at this time.

NASA does, however, encourage international students to explore certain NASA student challenges and citizen science projects.

Therefore, international students should monitor NASA’s official pages for other opportunities rather than assuming that the Spring 2027 OSTEM programme is open internationally.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The NASA Spring 2027 OSTEM Internship Program provides eligible students with an opportunity to gain paid, hands-on experience while contributing to projects connected to NASA’s mission.

The programme is designed for students at different stages of higher education and can accommodate a broad range of academic disciplines, including some non-STEM fields. Interns can develop technical and professional skills, gain practical workplace experience, work with NASA professionals, and strengthen their career readiness.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The current OSTEM programme requires applicants to be U.S. citizens, at least 16 years old, enrolled in an eligible programme at a U.S.-accredited institution, and have a minimum 3.0 GPA.

The deadline for the Spring 2027 NASA OSTEM Internship is September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Students who meet the requirements should begin reviewing the available opportunities and preparing their applications as early as possible.

Click HERE for more internship opportunities.
